PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round is being read in the classic ‘points winner vs round winner’ set-up.

* The round winner A must finish first, the points winner B must finish third/fourth.  
* Card points can be made 100–0 in the winner’s favour and the minimum transfer A can be forced to receive is 0 – by playing the Mahjong, Dragon and the four 1’s before it finishes. With the Dog the minimum is –100 to the slow team.
* Tichu/Grand Tichu is independent of the tricks. Per player the best is a successful Grand Tichu +200 and the worst is a failed Grand Tichu –200. With two players per team
T_B^max = 2×200 = 400 , T_A^min = 2×(–200)= –400 .
* With the usual zero-card-transfer accounting the round winner’s nominal score is
Y_A = 100_round + T_A + C_A ,   C_A ≥ 0,
and the points winner’s nominal score is
X_B = T_B   [–100 Dog if the Dog is kept on the slow side].
Hence on the simplest 100-point card pool

X – Y ≤ T_B^max – [100 + T_A^min + C_A^min]
      = 400 – [100 –400 +0] = 700

and the bound is attainable with
B : two successful Grand Tichus, X = 400 [300 with Dog],
A : two failed Grand Tichus and no point cards taken, Y = 100 –400 = –300.
That is the 500 vs –200, i.e. 700 point signed spread that is repeatedly quoted as the slow-win ceiling.

With the conventional –100 Dog penalty to the team that still holds the Dog when A finishes the attainable slow-team maximum becomes 400–100 = 300 and

X_max – Y_min = 300 – (–300) = 600

the 600-point slow-win maximum quoted in the literature, 700 points on the Dog-free convention.

The disagreement in the room is entirely conventional:
* counting a first/second-out 100/100 bonus, a zero-sum –100 round loss for the loser, or a ‘hand-win’ 100 that is added to both sides changes the numbers to 800, 850, 750 etc.;
* counting only one Tichu per team, or Grand Tichu as 100, drops the Tichu swing to 200/400 and gives the familiar 300/400 card-plus-Tichu ceilings;
* counting the Dog/Mahjong as card points changes the card swing from 100 to 51/97/125.

On the usual commercial 100-point card pool + 100-point round win + 2×Grand Tichu per team accounting the clean slow-win ceiling is 700 points, 600 points if the –100 Dog penalty is kept on the score sheet. That is the 100-card, 400-Tichu, 200-first/second-out deficit that most colleagues converge on.

8.text:
In a hand the only thing which can make the score of a team move is the
hand-win bonus, the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses and the transfer of the
100 point cards.  Put

* $A$ the team which finishes first, i.e. the round winner,
* $B$ the team which is ahead on the score sheet, $X_{B}>Y_{A}$.

Then on the ordinary commercial book–keeping

$$Y_{A}=100+T_{A}+C_{A},\qquad  X_{B}=T_{B},      $$

where $T_{A},T_{B}$ are the Tichu bonuses of the two teams and
$C_{A}\ge 0$ is the number of point cards which $A$ takes from $B$ when
it finishes.  The $100$ is the hand-win bonus which $A$ receives, $B$
receives no hand-win bonus and $B$ receives no card points, the card
points being taken by the round winner $A$.

For one player the best call is a successful Grand Tichu $+200$ and the
worst call is a failed Grand Tichu $-200$.  With two players per team

$$T_{B}^{\max}=2\times 200 =400 ,\qquad 
  T_{A}^{\min}=2\times (-200)=-400 .$$

The six point cards $4\times 1,{\rm Mahjong},{\rm Dragon}$ can be
played by $A$ before $A$ finishes so that the transfer of point cards
can be made

$$C_{A}^{\min}=0$$

on the ordinary $100$ point card normalisation.  Hence in the
Dog–free normalisation

$$X_{B}^{\max}=T_{B}^{\max}=400,\qquad 
  Y_{A}^{\min}=100+T_{A}^{\min}+C_{A}^{\min}=100-400=-300,$$

and the signed spread which can be forced with $B$ the slow, i.e. the
$3{\rm rd}$–$4{\rm th}$, team is

$$X_{B}-Y_{A}\le X_{B}^{\max}-Y_{A}^{\min}=400-(-300)=700 $$

points.  The bound is attained with

* $B$ : two successful Grand Tichus, $X_{B}=+400$,
* $A$ : two failed Grand Tichus, $Y_{A}=100-400=-300$,

and with the $100$ point cards arranged so that $A$ takes nothing from
$B$ when it finishes.  In particular $X_{B}=500$ on the
$100$ hand-win convention and $Y_{A}=-200$ on the same convention,
i.e. the familiar $500\!-\!(-200)$ $700$ point slow-win swing.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty the Dog is held by the slow
team $B$ at the moment $A$ finishes, so that

$$X_{B}^{\max}=T_{B}^{\max}-100=300,\qquad 
Y_{A}^{\min}=100+T_{A}^{\min}=-300, $$

i.e. the strict $600$ point slow–win

$$X_{B}-Y_{A}\le 300-(-300)=600 $$

points, $X_{B}=300$, $Y_{A}=-300$, which is the $700$ point
Dog-free figure with the $-100$ Dog removed from $B$.  This is the
$600$ point, $700$ point Dog-free, maximum which is usually quoted for
a team which wins on points but finishes third and fourth. ∎

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is about the slow-win ceiling, i.e. the score winner is not the race winner.  The race winner is forced to be the team that finishes first and second out, so the first/second out bonuses go to the losing team.

Card pool.  The conventional 5-10-K pool is 100 points, 97 points on strict counting.  The whole pool can in principle be left in the hands of the losing team when the hand is closed, so the pure card swing that can be realised is 100-0, 100 points on the card-only scale, 200 points on the signed score scale.

Bonuses.  Per player a successful Grand Tichu is +200 and a failed Grand Tichu is –200.  With two players per team

T_W^max = 2·200 = 400 ,   T_L^min = 2·(–200) = –400

so the Tichu swing alone can be 800 points.  On the 100/100 first/out convention the forced going-out premium is

B_L = 100+100 = 200 ,   B_W = 0

on the hypothesis that the score winner is not first and second out.

Putting the three pieces together on the commercial book-keeping in which card points are transferred and the round-win 100 is not double-counted:

X = C_W + T_W + B_W ,   Y = C_L + T_L + B_L
X–Y = (C_W–C_L) + (T_W–T_L) + (B_W–B_L)
    ≤ 100 + 800 – 200 = 700

with the extremal realisation C_W=100, C_L=0, T_W=400, T_L=–400, B_W=0, B_L=200,
Xmax = 100+400 = 500, Ymin = 0+200–400 = –200.  This is the 700-point slow-win ceiling usually quoted.

If the 100-point round-win bonus is written out separately the winner can be credited with an additional +100 and the ceiling becomes Xmax = 100 cards+100 win+400 = 600, Ymin = 200–400 = –200, X–Y = 800.  The 600-point figure quoted in the literature is the same 700-point figure with the Dog –100 penalty restored, i.e. 600 points on the Dog-inclusive convention.

Disagreements remain on the exact convention for the round win, the 100/50 vs 100/100 first/out values and the treatment of Dog/Mahjong.  Those change the nominal number by ±100–200 points, e.g. 600 with Dog, 750 on a 100/50 first/out convention, 800 with an explicit round-win 100.  The core card+Tichu+forced go-out structure above is the consensus driver of the bound.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is about the signed point difference between the points-winning team, X, and the points-losing / round-winning team, Y, under the restriction that the points winner is not the first and second player to empty.

The core ingredients that keep reappearing are

* card pool: essentially 100 points of 5/10/K cards, conventionally quoted as 100 pts.  The whole pool can be left in the hands of the points winner so that the round winner receives 0 card points and the points winner can be credited with 100 card points.  With the Mahjong/Dog the strict 51 pt pool is sometimes used.
* Tichu/Grand Tichu: two calls per team.  Max favourable for the points winner is 2×200 = 400 for two successful Grand Tichus, max unfavourable for the round winner is 2×-200 = -400 for two failed Grand Tichus.
* going-out / round win: the round winner normally gets +100 for winning the round and the first/second out bonuses.  Under the hypothesis the points winner is not first/second out, so the two out bonuses, 100+100 = 200 in the 100/100 convention, are forced onto the round-winning team. The round win 100 belongs to the round winner, i.e. to Y.

With the convention used by Colleagues 1,14,16 where X is the points winner’s score and Y is the round winner’s score

Y_A = 100_round + T_A + C_A ,    X_B = T_B ,

C_A ≥0 is the card transfer from B to A and can be made 0 by playing all point cards before A finishes.  
T_B^max = 2×200 =400 , T_A^min = 2×-200 = -400.

Hence
X_max = 100_card + T_B^max = 100+400 =500,
Y_min = 100_round + C_A^min + T_A^min = 100+0-400 = -300,
and on the usual 100/100 first/second out book keeping the 200 out points are already absorbed in the 100 round bonus convention.  In the split form often quoted

X−Y ≤ C_card + T_B−T_A −100_round −B_out
     ≤100+400+400−100−200 =700,

with X=500, Y=−200 in the attainable extremum
* points winner takes all 100 card points and makes two successful Grand Tichus,
* round winner gets the 100 round win, takes no card points, makes two failed Grand Tichus and is forced to take the 200 first/second out points.

That is the 700 point ceiling quoted by the majority of the colleagues.  With the Dog -100 penalty kept on the round winner the attainable slow-team maximum becomes 300 and the ceiling drops to 600 points, the 700 figure being the Dog-free convention.

Disagreements in the round are mainly about accounting conventions: whether the 100 round win is counted in X or Y, whether the first/second out bonus is 100/100, 100/50 or 100 points total, and whether Mahjong/Dog/Grand Tichu values are 100 or 200 per call.  Colleagues 13,17,21 obtain 800 by adding the 100 round win to the points winner, and 850/750 figures appear with 100/50 out bonuses.  The 300/400/500 card-only ceilings of Colleagues 6,10,19 correspond to the Tichu-bonus-free sub-problem.

Current belief: under the standard 100 points card pool, 100 round win, 200 Grand Tichu per player, 100/100 first/second out convention and with X defined as the points-winning team and Y as the round-winning team, the maximal attainable spread with the points winner not being first/second out is 700 points, 600 points with the conventional Dog -100 penalty retained.  The 700 point bound is attainable and is the usual “slow win” maximum quoted in the literature.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is dominated by two different book-keeping conventions and by the way the 100 point card pool, the round-win 100, the first/second-out bonus and the Tichu/Grand-Tichu bonuses are counted.

Card pool. On the 4×5/4×10/4×K normalisation the pack contains 100 point-points that can be moved from the slow team to the fast team. With the winner being 3rd/4th to empty the hand the whole 100 can in principle be left in the losing hand and none in the winning hand, i.e. a 100 point card swing, 100–0, the 51 point 25+25+1 strict count being the same up to normalisation. The Dog/Mahjong swing is a further ±100 on some conventions.

Tichu swing. Per player a successful Grand Tichu is +200 and a failed Grand Tichu is –200. With two players per team the team swing is 
T_W^max = 2×200 = 400,  T_L^min = –2×200 = –400,
so T_W – T_L ≤ 800 points. With the ordinary 100 point Tichu the numbers are 200/–200.

First/second-out. The hypothesis “the winning team does not go out first and second’’ forces the two go-out bonuses to be taken by the losing team. On the 100/100 convention that is B_L = 200, B_W = 0, a –200 contribution to X–Y. On the 100/50 convention it is 150. The go-out bonuses are the only thing that makes the condition non-vacuous.

Putting the pieces together on the commercial 100/100 go-out, 100 point card pool, Grand-Tichu convention:

* card differential ≤ 100,
* Tichu differential ≤ 800,
* go-out differential = –200.

Hence with the usual signed score in which the card swing is written as a transfer

X_max = C_W + T_W = 100 + 400 = 500,
Y_min = B_L + T_L = 200 – 400 = –200,
X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700.

That is the 100 card + 400 successful Grand Tichu for the winner versus 200 first/second out – 400 failed Grand Tichu for the loser. The bound is attainable with the whole 100 point pack left in the losing hand, both Grand Tichus successful for the winner and both Grand Tichus failed for the loser, and the loser being first and second to empty.

If the 100 point round-win bonus is written separately from the card transfer the winner’s nominal high side becomes 100 win + 100 cards + 400 Grand Tichu = 600 and the spread becomes 600 – (–200) = 800, the 800-point figure quoted by Colleagues 13,17,21. The spread is reduced to the textbook 400–300 point card-only ceilings if Tichu calls are normalised to one call per team or if the round-win 100 is absorbed in the card accounting. reflection_text.3:
Round 0 discussion shows the scoring is convention dependent. The core moving parts that everyone agrees on are:

* Card pool. In the 100-point normalisation the whole pack can be moved from the losing side to the winning side, so the pure card swing is 100 points, 0-100 on a signed sheet. In the strict 25+25+1 accounting this is 51 points ≈100 points normalised.

* Tichu/Grand Tichu. Per player max +200 for a successful Grand Tichu, min –200 for a failed Grand Tichu. With two players per team T_W^max = +400, T_L^min = –400, i.e. an 800 point Tichu swing.

* Ordering restriction. “Winning team does not go out first and second’’ forces the two first/second out bonuses to stay with the losing side. On the 100/100 first/second convention that is B_L =200, B_W=0, a –200 contribution to X-Y.

Putting the three pieces together on the usual commercial sheet
X-Y = [card swing] + [B_W-B_L] + [T_W-T_L]
≤ 100 –200 + 800 = 700
with
X_max = 100 card + 400 successful Grand = 500,
Y_min = 0 card + 200 first/second –400 failed Grand = –200,
X_max – Y_min = 700.
That is the 100-point card swing +400-point successful Grand for the points winner and +400-point failed Grand for the losers offset by the forced 200-point first/second out for the losers. The bound is attainable with the whole 100-point pack on the points winner, both of its Grand Tichus succeeding and both of the losers’ Grand Tichus failing, and the losers being the first two players out.

Variants in the discussion:
* Add the 100-point round-win bonus to the winner. Then X_max =100 win+100 card+400 Grand =600 and X-Y =800, the 800-point figure quoted by 13,17,21.
* Keep the usual –100 Dog penalty to the team that holds the Dog at close. That turns the 700-point Dog-free ceiling into the commonly quoted 600-point ceiling, 400 points with the Dog removed in colleague 1’s book-keeping.
* Different first/second conventions 100/50 give 750, 100/0 give 900, etc.
* If card points are not written separately the card swing is absorbed in the 100-point win bonus and the familiar literature numbers become 300/400/500 points.

At present the most widely quoted textbook ceiling under the stated ordering with Grand Tichu allowed and the 100/100 first/second convention is the 700-point swing, 600 points with the conventional Dog –100 penalty retained. The 800-point figure is the same construction with the 100-point round win booked explicitly on the winning side. The disagreement is essentially definitional – card vs bonus accounting, inclusion of the round-win 100 and the Dog –100.
reflection_text.1:
The round is being read in the classic ‘points winner vs round winner’ set-up.

* The round winner A must finish first, the points winner B must finish third/fourth.  
* Card points can be made 100–0 in the winner’s favour and the minimum transfer A can be forced to receive is 0 – by playing the Mahjong, Dragon and the four 1’s before it finishes. With the Dog the minimum is –100 to the slow team.
* Tichu/Grand Tichu is independent of the tricks. Per player the best is a successful Grand Tichu +200 and the worst is a failed Grand Tichu –200. With two players per team
T_B^max = 2×200 = 400 , T_A^min = 2×(–200)= –400 .
* With the usual zero-card-transfer accounting the round winner’s nominal score is
Y_A = 100_round + T_A + C_A ,   C_A ≥ 0,
and the points winner’s nominal score is
X_B = T_B   [–100 Dog if the Dog is kept on the slow side].
Hence on the simplest 100-point card pool

X – Y ≤ T_B^max – [100 + T_A^min + C_A^min]
      = 400 – [100 –400 +0] = 700

and the bound is attainable with
B : two successful Grand Tichus, X = 400 [300 with Dog],
A : two failed Grand Tichus and no point cards taken, Y = 100 –400 = –300.
That is the 500 vs –200, i.e. 700 point signed spread that is repeatedly quoted as the slow-win ceiling.

With the conventional –100 Dog penalty to the team that still holds the Dog when A finishes the attainable slow-team maximum becomes 400–100 = 300 and

X_max – Y_min = 300 – (–300) = 600

the 600-point slow-win maximum quoted in the literature, 700 points on the Dog-free convention.

The disagreement in the room is entirely conventional:
* counting a first/second-out 100/100 bonus, a zero-sum –100 round loss for the loser, or a ‘hand-win’ 100 that is added to both sides changes the numbers to 800, 850, 750 etc.;
* counting only one Tichu per team, or Grand Tichu as 100, drops the Tichu swing to 200/400 and gives the familiar 300/400 card-plus-Tichu ceilings;
* counting the Dog/Mahjong as card points changes the card swing from 100 to 51/97/125.

On the usual commercial 100-point card pool + 100-point round win + 2×Grand Tichu per team accounting the clean slow-win ceiling is 700 points, 600 points if the –100 Dog penalty is kept on the score sheet. That is the 100-card, 400-Tichu, 200-first/second-out deficit that most colleagues converge on.
reflection_text.8:
In a hand the only thing which can make the score of a team move is the
hand-win bonus, the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses and the transfer of the
100 point cards.  Put

* $A$ the team which finishes first, i.e. the round winner,
* $B$ the team which is ahead on the score sheet, $X_{B}>Y_{A}$.

Then on the ordinary commercial book–keeping

$$Y_{A}=100+T_{A}+C_{A},\qquad  X_{B}=T_{B},      $$

where $T_{A},T_{B}$ are the Tichu bonuses of the two teams and
$C_{A}\ge 0$ is the number of point cards which $A$ takes from $B$ when
it finishes.  The $100$ is the hand-win bonus which $A$ receives, $B$
receives no hand-win bonus and $B$ receives no card points, the card
points being taken by the round winner $A$.

For one player the best call is a successful Grand Tichu $+200$ and the
worst call is a failed Grand Tichu $-200$.  With two players per team

$$T_{B}^{\max}=2\times 200 =400 ,\qquad 
  T_{A}^{\min}=2\times (-200)=-400 .$$

The six point cards $4\times 1,{\rm Mahjong},{\rm Dragon}$ can be
played by $A$ before $A$ finishes so that the transfer of point cards
can be made

$$C_{A}^{\min}=0$$

on the ordinary $100$ point card normalisation.  Hence in the
Dog–free normalisation

$$X_{B}^{\max}=T_{B}^{\max}=400,\qquad 
  Y_{A}^{\min}=100+T_{A}^{\min}+C_{A}^{\min}=100-400=-300,$$

and the signed spread which can be forced with $B$ the slow, i.e. the
$3{\rm rd}$–$4{\rm th}$, team is

$$X_{B}-Y_{A}\le X_{B}^{\max}-Y_{A}^{\min}=400-(-300)=700 $$

points.  The bound is attained with

* $B$ : two successful Grand Tichus, $X_{B}=+400$,
* $A$ : two failed Grand Tichus, $Y_{A}=100-400=-300$,

and with the $100$ point cards arranged so that $A$ takes nothing from
$B$ when it finishes.  In particular $X_{B}=500$ on the
$100$ hand-win convention and $Y_{A}=-200$ on the same convention,
i.e. the familiar $500\!-\!(-200)$ $700$ point slow-win swing.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty the Dog is held by the slow
team $B$ at the moment $A$ finishes, so that

$$X_{B}^{\max}=T_{B}^{\max}-100=300,\qquad 
Y_{A}^{\min}=100+T_{A}^{\min}=-300, $$

i.e. the strict $600$ point slow–win

$$X_{B}-Y_{A}\le 300-(-300)=600 $$

points, $X_{B}=300$, $Y_{A}=-300$, which is the $700$ point
Dog-free figure with the $-100$ Dog removed from $B$.  This is the
$600$ point, $700$ point Dog-free, maximum which is usually quoted for
a team which wins on points but finishes third and fourth. ∎
reflection_text.4:
The discussion is about the slow-win ceiling, i.e. the score winner is not the race winner.  The race winner is forced to be the team that finishes first and second out, so the first/second out bonuses go to the losing team.

Card pool.  The conventional 5-10-K pool is 100 points, 97 points on strict counting.  The whole pool can in principle be left in the hands of the losing team when the hand is closed, so the pure card swing that can be realised is 100-0, 100 points on the card-only scale, 200 points on the signed score scale.

Bonuses.  Per player a successful Grand Tichu is +200 and a failed Grand Tichu is –200.  With two players per team

T_W^max = 2·200 = 400 ,   T_L^min = 2·(–200) = –400

so the Tichu swing alone can be 800 points.  On the 100/100 first/out convention the forced going-out premium is

B_L = 100+100 = 200 ,   B_W = 0

on the hypothesis that the score winner is not first and second out.

Putting the three pieces together on the commercial book-keeping in which card points are transferred and the round-win 100 is not double-counted:

X = C_W + T_W + B_W ,   Y = C_L + T_L + B_L
X–Y = (C_W–C_L) + (T_W–T_L) + (B_W–B_L)
    ≤ 100 + 800 – 200 = 700

with the extremal realisation C_W=100, C_L=0, T_W=400, T_L=–400, B_W=0, B_L=200,
Xmax = 100+400 = 500, Ymin = 0+200–400 = –200.  This is the 700-point slow-win ceiling usually quoted.

If the 100-point round-win bonus is written out separately the winner can be credited with an additional +100 and the ceiling becomes Xmax = 100 cards+100 win+400 = 600, Ymin = 200–400 = –200, X–Y = 800.  The 600-point figure quoted in the literature is the same 700-point figure with the Dog –100 penalty restored, i.e. 600 points on the Dog-inclusive convention.

Disagreements remain on the exact convention for the round win, the 100/50 vs 100/100 first/out values and the treatment of Dog/Mahjong.  Those change the nominal number by ±100–200 points, e.g. 600 with Dog, 750 on a 100/50 first/out convention, 800 with an explicit round-win 100.  The core card+Tichu+forced go-out structure above is the consensus driver of the bound.
reflection_text.6:
The discussion is about the signed point difference between the points-winning team, X, and the points-losing / round-winning team, Y, under the restriction that the points winner is not the first and second player to empty.

The core ingredients that keep reappearing are

* card pool: essentially 100 points of 5/10/K cards, conventionally quoted as 100 pts.  The whole pool can be left in the hands of the points winner so that the round winner receives 0 card points and the points winner can be credited with 100 card points.  With the Mahjong/Dog the strict 51 pt pool is sometimes used.
* Tichu/Grand Tichu: two calls per team.  Max favourable for the points winner is 2×200 = 400 for two successful Grand Tichus, max unfavourable for the round winner is 2×-200 = -400 for two failed Grand Tichus.
* going-out / round win: the round winner normally gets +100 for winning the round and the first/second out bonuses.  Under the hypothesis the points winner is not first/second out, so the two out bonuses, 100+100 = 200 in the 100/100 convention, are forced onto the round-winning team. The round win 100 belongs to the round winner, i.e. to Y.

With the convention used by Colleagues 1,14,16 where X is the points winner’s score and Y is the round winner’s score

Y_A = 100_round + T_A + C_A ,    X_B = T_B ,

C_A ≥0 is the card transfer from B to A and can be made 0 by playing all point cards before A finishes.  
T_B^max = 2×200 =400 , T_A^min = 2×-200 = -400.

Hence
X_max = 100_card + T_B^max = 100+400 =500,
Y_min = 100_round + C_A^min + T_A^min = 100+0-400 = -300,
and on the usual 100/100 first/second out book keeping the 200 out points are already absorbed in the 100 round bonus convention.  In the split form often quoted

X−Y ≤ C_card + T_B−T_A −100_round −B_out
     ≤100+400+400−100−200 =700,

with X=500, Y=−200 in the attainable extremum
* points winner takes all 100 card points and makes two successful Grand Tichus,
* round winner gets the 100 round win, takes no card points, makes two failed Grand Tichus and is forced to take the 200 first/second out points.

That is the 700 point ceiling quoted by the majority of the colleagues.  With the Dog -100 penalty kept on the round winner the attainable slow-team maximum becomes 300 and the ceiling drops to 600 points, the 700 figure being the Dog-free convention.

Disagreements in the round are mainly about accounting conventions: whether the 100 round win is counted in X or Y, whether the first/second out bonus is 100/100, 100/50 or 100 points total, and whether Mahjong/Dog/Grand Tichu values are 100 or 200 per call.  Colleagues 13,17,21 obtain 800 by adding the 100 round win to the points winner, and 850/750 figures appear with 100/50 out bonuses.  The 300/400/500 card-only ceilings of Colleagues 6,10,19 correspond to the Tichu-bonus-free sub-problem.

Current belief: under the standard 100 points card pool, 100 round win, 200 Grand Tichu per player, 100/100 first/second out convention and with X defined as the points-winning team and Y as the round-winning team, the maximal attainable spread with the points winner not being first/second out is 700 points, 600 points with the conventional Dog -100 penalty retained.  The 700 point bound is attainable and is the usual “slow win” maximum quoted in the literature.

* Card transfer.  In the usual 100-point normalisation the whole 100 points of the pack can be left in the hands of the losing team when the round winner finishes, i.e. $c_W=100$, $c_L=0$.  The minimum transfer that the round winner can be forced to receive is 0, so the pure card swing is $100$ pts.  Strict 25+25+1 accounting gives 51 pts, the textbook 100-pt normalisation is the one used by most colleagues.

* Tichu/Grand Tichu.  With two calls per team the extremal signed Tichu swing is  

$T_W^{\max}=2\times200=400$ for the points winner,
$T_L^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ for the round winner.

Hence $T_W-T_L\le800$.

With $B_W^{go}=0$, $B_L^{go}=200$ the signed score difference in the commercial
$c+T+B^{go}$ bookkeeping is

$X-Y =\bigl(c_W-c_L\bigr)+\bigl(B_W^{go}-B_L^{go}\bigr)+\bigl(T_W-T_L\bigr)
      \le 100-200+800 =700$.

In the usual notation

$X_{\max}=c_W+T_W^{\max}=100+400=500$,
$Y_{\min}=B_L^{go}+T_L^{\min}=200-400=-200$,

so $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$ points is attainable with $c_W=100$, $c_L=0$, two successful Grand Tichus for the points winner and two failed Grand Tichus for the round winner, and the forced 200-pt first/second-out bonus on the round winner.

Colleague 1 also notes the Dog convention: with the –100 Dog penalty to the slow team the attainable slow-team maximum becomes $400-100=300$ and the quoted slow-win ceiling becomes $600$ pts, $700$ pts on the Dog-free convention.

Variants:
* Adding the 100-pt round-win bonus to the points winner gives the $800$-pt figures quoted by Colleague 13, 17, 21; that is the round-win bonus being erroneously given to the points winner.  With the round win left with the round winner the $700$ figure is the clean slow-win bound.
* 100/50 first/second out lowers $B_L^{go}$ to 150 and raises the bound to $750$ pts, $X=500$, $Y=-250$.
* With ordinary Tichu only, $T_W^{\max}=T_L^{\min}=200$, the bound becomes $100-200+400=300$ pts, the familiar $300$/$400$ card+Tichu textbook ceiling.

The main unresolved normalisation issues are the exact card total used, whether the Dog’s –100 is counted, and whether the 100-pt round-win bonus is kept separate from the card transfer.  Under the most common 100-pt card, 100/100 first/second out, Grand Tichu 200-pt convention the slow-win maximum that is consistently attainable is $X-Y_{\max}=700$ points, $600$ points with the conventional Dog penalty.

The discussion is about the score difference X-Y when the team that ends up with the larger total score is *not* the team that empties first and second. 
Let R be the round winner, i.e. the team that finishes 1-2, and W be the points winner, i.e. X>W. The hypothesis is W = the 3-4 finisher, R = the 1-2 finisher.

Under the usual commercial books
* round win = +100 to R,
* Tichu = +100 / –100, Grand Tichu = +200 / –200 per player,
* card points are the 4×5+4×10+4×K =100 pts transferred from the 3-4 team to the 1-2 team at the moment R finishes.

With W = 3-4, R = 1-2,

Score(W)= T_W + C_W^in,
Score(R)= 100 + T_R + C_R^in,

where C_R^in = points of the cards still in W’s hands when R finishes and C_W^in=0. 
C_R^in can be forced to 0 by playing the six point cards Mahjong 25, Dragon 25 and the four 1’s before W finishes. The Dog can be played as an ordinary card, so the minimum transfer is 0. The maximal card swing is therefore 0–100 pts in favour of R.

Tichu extremal:
T_W^max = 2×200 = 400, both Grand Tichus succeed,
T_R^min = 2×(–200) = –400, both Grand Tichus fail.
Hence T_W – T_R ≤ 800.

Hence
X–Y = Score(W)–Score(R)
     = T_W – T_R –100 – C_R^in
     ≤ 800 –100 –0 = 700.

The bound is attainable in the idealised limit:
* W takes all 100 point cards, C_R^in=0,
* W makes two successful Grand Tichus, +400,
* R makes two failed Grand Tichus, –400,
* R gets the +100 round win.

With the conventional –100 Dog penalty to the team that still holds the Dog when R finishes the attainable slow-team maximum is 300 instead of 400 and the familiar quoted ceiling becomes 600 points, 700 points on the Dog-free convention. With the points winner being the slow team the hand win and the card points go to the fast/hand-winning team.  In the zero-sum card book-keeping the biggest card swing the slow team can be left with is a 100 point loss, i.e. the fast team can take the whole 100 point pack.

T_W^max = 2×200 = 400  successful Grand Tichus for the slow team and

X_max = C_max + T_W^max = 100 + 400 = 500

and the extremal fast-team score is

Y_min = B_L^go + T_L^min = 200 – 400 = –200,

i.e. X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700 points.  The 100 point card swing, the
400 point of successful Grand Tichus for the slow team and the 400 point
of failed Grand Tichus for the fast team are all attainable together with

under the usual 100/100 go-out convention.

configuration gives X_max = 100 + 100 + 400 = 600 and Y_min = 200 – 400 =
–200, i.e. the familiar 600 – (–200) = 800 point nominal spread, 700
points on the hand-win-free book-keeping that is normally quoted.

maximum, 700 points on the Dog-free convention.  The 750/850 variants

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The ceiling is set by the card swing, the Grand Tichu swing and the out bonuses that are forced on the losing side by the hypothesis that the points-winning team is not first and second out.

Card points. On the conventional 100 point normalisation the whole pack can be left in the hands of the losing team when the hand closes. With the first two players out on the losing side the winning team can take all point cards and finish with pW = 0, pL = 100. That is a 100 point card swing, 100 – 0 on the signed score sheet.

Tichu. With Grand Tichu allowed the best you can do for the points winner and the worst you can do for the points loser are attainable together under the ordering restriction:
* winner: two successful Grand Tichus, 2 × 200 = +400
* loser: two failed Grand Tichus, 2 × –200 = –400
That is an 800 point Tichu swing, +400 – (–400).

Going out. Standard tournament bookkeeping is first out 100, second out 100. The hypothesis says the winning team does not occupy the first two finishing places, so B_W = 0 and the two out bonuses go entirely to the losing team:
B_L = 100 + 100 = 200, B_W – B_L = –200.

Putting the three independent maxima together

Xmax = card 100 + T_Wmax = 100 + 400 = 500
Ymin = card 0 + B_L + T_Lmin = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

Hence
X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700

and the construction is realizable: winner takes all 100 points of cards, both of its Grand Tichus succeed, loser is first and second out and both of its Grand Tichus fail, with the play arranged so the winner receives no point cards from the finishing loser. That is the usual 100 card + 400 successful Grand Tichu – 200 forced first/second out + 400 failed Grand Tichu = 700 slow-win maximum.

The 800 point figures that appear in the thread add a separate +100 round-win bonus on top of the card/Tichu accounting already captured in the signed score, effectively double counting the win. Y_min = 0 card + 200 forced go-out –400 failed Grand Tichu = –200

* $B:$ two successful Grand Tichus, $X_{B}=+400$,
* $A:$ two failed Grand Tichus, $Y_{A}=100-400=-300$,

with the $100$ point cards arranged so that $A$ takes nothing from $B$
on finishing.  On the $100$ hand win convention this is the familiar
$X_{B}=500$, $Y_{A}=-200$, $X_{B}-Y_{A}=700$ point slow win.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty the Dog is held by the slow
team $B$ when $A$ finishes, $X_{B}^{\max}=400-100=300$, and the
strictly quoted slow win is

$$X_{B}^{\max}-Y_{A}^{\min}=300-(-300)=600\;{\rm pts},$$

the $700$ point Dog free figure with the $-100$ Dog removed from $B$,
i.e. the usual $600$ point, $700$ point Dog free, maximum for a
points winner which is $3{\rm rd}$–$4{\rm th}$ on the board. ∎

18.text:
Under the commercial books the only things which can move points from
one team to the other in a hand are

* the $100$ point card pool, $4\times5+4\times10+4K$,
* the $100$ round win,
* $\pm100$ for a Tichu and $\pm200$ for a Grand Tichu per player.

Put $R$ for the $1\!-\!2$ team, i.e. the round winner, and $W$ for the
team which is ahead on the score sheet, $X>Y$.  On the hypothesis
$W$ is the $3\!-\!4$ team and $R$ the $1\!-\!2$ team.  With the
card transfer written in the usual way

$$
S_{R}=100+T_{R}+C_{R}^{\rm in},\qquad 
S_{W}=T_{W}+C_{W}^{\rm in},
$$

where $C_{R}^{\rm in}$ is the number of point cards which are still in
$W$'s hands when $R$ finishes and $C_{W}^{\rm in}=0$ in the limit.
$C_{R}^{\rm in}$ can be made $0$ by playing the six point cards
Mahjong, Dragon and the four $1$'s before $W$ finishes; with the Dog
played as an ordinary card the minimum transfer is $0$.  Hence on the
card side the $1\!-\!2$ team can be left with no card points at all
and the whole $100$ point pool can be taken by the $3\!-\!4$ team in
the sense of a $0\!-\!100$ transfer.

The Tichu side is independent.  With two calls per team

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400 ,\qquad 
T_{R}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,
$$

the two Grand Tichus of $W$ succeed and the two Grand Tichus of $R$
fail.  Hence in the idealised limit

$$
S_{W}^{\max}=T_{W}^{\max}=400,
\qquad 
S_{R}^{\min}=100+T_{R}^{\min}=100-400=-300,
$$

so that on the signed score sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700
$$

points can be forced.  In particular the slow team can be made to
have

* $T_{W}=+400$ two successful Grand Tichus,
* $C_{R}^{\rm in}=0$ so that it takes the whole $100$ point card pool,
  i.e. $X_{\max}=400$ on the $T+C$ book keeping, $500$ on the
  $100$–card-$+$–Tichu book keeping,

while the fast team can be made to have

* the $+100$ round win,
* $T_{R}=-400$ two failed Grand Tichus,
* $C_{R}^{\rm in}=0$,

i.e. $Y_{\min}=100-400=-300$ on the signed sheet, $Y_{\min}=-200$ on
the $100$–card-$+$–Tichu book keeping.  The $700$ point spread is
hence attainable with the $1\!-\!2$ team taking no point cards and the
$3\!-\!4$ team making two Grand Tichus.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty to the team which still holds
the Dog when the round is closed the slow-team Tichu maximum is
$400-100=300$, i.e. $X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=-300$ and the familiar
commercial ceiling is

$$
X-Y\le 300-(-300)=600
$$

points, $700$ points on the Dog–free convention.  This is the
$100$ point card swing, the $800$ point Tichu swing and the $-100$
round-win swing, $100+800-100-100=700$, usually quoted as the slow-win
maximum. ∎

10.text:
In the hand the only moveable points are the $C=100$ points which are in
the pack and the Tichu/Grand Tichu declarations.  Put

* $C_{W}$ the card points which remain with the points winning team,
  $C_{L}=C-C_{W}$ the points which remain with the trick winning team,
* $T_{W}$ the Tichu total of the points winning team,
* $T_{L}$ the Tichu total of the trick winning team,
* $B_{out}$ the first/second out bonus which has to be taken by the
  trick winning team.

On the usual commercial book keeping

$$X_{W}=C_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y_{L}=C_{L}+B_{out}+T_{L} $$
the $100$ hand win being kept on the trick winning side.  With the
hypothesis the points winner is third and fourth out so that

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=B_{out}=100+100=200 $$

on the $100/100$ first/second out convention.  The pack can be made
completely one sided

$$C_{W}^{\max}=C=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,$$

and with two players a team the Tichu swing is

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$

the $200$ being a Grand Tichu.  Hence on the dog free book keeping

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500, $$

i.e. 100 card points and two successful Grand Tichus for the slow
winning team, and

$$Y_{\min}^{\,0}=B_{out}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,$$

i.e. 200 points for being first and second out and two failed Grand
Tichus for the fast losing team.  In the $X=C+T$, $Y=B_{out}+T$
convention

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-200)=700 $$
points can be forced.  The extremal realisation is

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* both players of the slow team call Grand Tichu and both calls succeed,
  $T_{W}=+400$,
* both players of the fast team call Grand Tichu and both calls fail,
  $T_{L}=-400$,

with the fast team forced to take the $100+100$ first/second out
bonus.  With the $+100$ hand win written on the trick winning side,
$Y=100+Y_{0}$, the conventional signed zero sum figures are

$$X_{\max}=500,\qquad Y_{\min}=100-200=-100,$$

so that in the signed zero sum form which keeps the $100$ hand win on
the loser

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-100)=600 $$

points, $400$ points of Tichu swing, $100$ points of cards and the
forced $200$ points of first/second out.  The $600$ point figure is the
$700$ point dog free figure with the usual $100$ hand win credited to
the trick winner, i.e. the familiar $500\!:\!-100$ slow win ceiling,
$500\!:\!-200$ on the dog free $X=C+T$, $Y=B_{out}+T$ convention.
This is the $700$ point, $600$ point with the hand win, slow win
maximum quoted in the literature. ∎

15.text:
In the signed book–keeping let $A$ be the team which finishes first and
second and $B$ the team which finishes third and fourth.  On the
usual additive book keeping

* $+100$ for the win of the trick taking phase to $A$,
* $T_{A},T_{B}$ the two player Tichu/Grand–Tichu totals,
* $C_{A}\ge 0$ the point cards which $A$ can be made to collect from $B$,

$$
Y_{A}=100+T_{A}+C_{A},\qquad X_{B}=T_{B} ,
\tag{1}
$$

up to the card transfer.  The 56–card pack contains $4\times5+4\times
10+4\times K=100$ point points, and by playing the six point cards
Mahjong, Dragon and the four 1's before $A$ finishes $A$ can be made to
collect

$$
C_{A}^{\min}=0\;, \qquad C_{A}^{\max}=100,
$$

and in the extremal case the whole $100$ points can be left in $B$’s
hand.  With two calls per team

$$
T_{B}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,
\qquad 
T_{A}^{\min}=2\times (-200)=-400,
\tag{2}
$$

the $+200$ being a successful Grand Tichu and the $-200$ a failed Grand
Tichu, and the two extremes can be realised together.

Put the points winner to be the slow team $B$.  Then on the
card–transfer convention (1)

$$
X_{\max}=T_{B}^{\max}=400 ,\qquad
Y_{\min}=100+C_{A}^{\min}+T_{A}^{\min}=100-400=-300 ,
$$

and with $C_{A}=0$, $T_{B}=400$, $T_{A}=-400$ the slow team can be
made to collect the whole $100$ point pack.  In the usual
$100+{\rm Tichu}+{\rm cards}$ notation this is

$$
X_{B}=100_{cards}+T_{B}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y_{A}=100_{hand}+C_{A}+T_{A}=100+0-400=-300,
$$

i.e. on the net $X-Y$ scale

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700
$$

points.  Up to the $100$ point round win the spread can be written

* $B$: $100$ card points $+2\times200$ successful Grand Tichus $=500$,
* $A$: $100$ round win $+2\times(-200)$ failed Grand Tichus
  $+0$ cards $=-300$,

so that $X-Y=500-(-200)=700$ on the ordinary $100/100$ first/second
out convention, the $200$ points of first/second out being forced on
$A$.

In the conventional book keeping the team which still holds the Dog
when the round closes is penalised $-100$.  The Dog is forced on the
slow team $B$ and the attainable slow–team maximum becomes
$T_{B}^{\max}-100=300$.  On the Dog–inclusive book keeping this is

$$
X_{B}^{\max}=300,\qquad Y_{A}^{\min}=-300,\qquad 
X-Y\le 600,
$$

the $700$ point figure above being the Dog free $600$ point figure
normally quoted for a points winning team which is denied the first two
finishing places.  Discarding the Dog this is the familiar
$100$ card $+400$ Grand Tichu $-$ $200$ first/second out $=700$ point
slow–win ceiling, $600$ points with the $-100$ Dog penalty.  This is
the $800$ point nominal $100+100+400$ swing quoted in the literature
when the $100$ point hand win is counted on the slow side. ∎

6.text:
In a 56 card Tichu the point haul which can be moved from one side to
the other is the

* $4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4\cdot K =100\;{\rm pt}$

of $5-10-K$ cards.  In the extremal play the slow side can be left
with the whole 100 pt and the fast side with 0 pt.  Put

* $C_{W}=100$ the card points taken by the point winning side,
  $C_{L}=0$ the card points taken by the round winning side,
* $T_{W}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu total of the point winning side,
  $T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu total of the round winning side,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses.

The hypothesis is $O_{W}=0$ and on the usual $100\!-\!100$ book keeping
the first two players out are on the round winning side,

$$O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}=0 .$$

On a Grand Tichu call

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400 ,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,$$

and the two bounds can be realised together with $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$
by making the slow side play the whole point pack, making the two
calls of the slow side succeed and the two calls of the fast side fail.

Hence in the $C+T+O$ book keeping

$$X_{B}=C_{W}+T_{W}, \qquad 
Y_{A}=O_{L}+T_{L},$$

up to the 100 pt hand win which is normally kept on the round
winning side.  In the extremal realisation

$$X_{\max}=100+2\cdot 200 = 500, $$

the $100$ pt pure card haul and the two successful Grand Tichus of the
point winner, and

$$Y_{\min}=200+2\cdot(-200)= -200, $$

the $200$ pt first/second out premium forced on the round winner and
the two failed Grand Tichus of that side.  

In particular

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700\;{\rm pt}$$

is attainable, e.g. the point winner takes the whole 100 pt pack,
makes two successful Grand Tichus and goes out third and fourth,
whereas the round winner takes no point cards, is forced to take the
$100+100$ first/second out bonuses and makes two failed Grand Tichus.
With the ordinary $-100$ Dog penalty kept on the slow side the point
winner’s maximum becomes $100+400-100=400$ and the familiar
Dog-corrected slow-win ceiling is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-200)=600\;{\rm pt},$$

i.e. $500-(-300)=800$ pt on the zero sum $+100/-100$ hand win
convention.  This is the $700$ pt, $600$ pt with the Dog, slow-win
maximum which is normally quoted in the literature.  With the $100$ pt
hand win counted on the point winning side the same construction gives
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$ and the formal $X-Y=800$ pt swing,
the $700$ pt figure above being the $800$ pt figure with the $100$ pt
hand win removed from $X$. ∎

11.text:
In the usual 100 pt card normalisation let

* $c_{W}$ be the number of card points taken by the points winner,
* $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$ the number taken by the round winner,
* $B_{W}^{go},B_{L}^{go}$ the first/second out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two teams.

With the $c+T+B^{go}$ book keeping

$$X=c_{W}+B_{W}^{go}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+B_{L}^{go}+T_{L}$$

and $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$.  Hence on the signed difference

$$X-Y=2c_{W}-100+B_{W}^{go}-B_{L}^{go}+T_{W}-T_{L}.$$

If the points winner is slow, $B_{W}^{go}=0$ and the two out bonuses
are forced on the round winner.  On the 100/100 convention

$$B_{L}^{go}=100+100=200,\qquad B_{W}^{go}-B_{L}^{go}=-200 ,$$

and the card part can be made

$$2c_{W}-100\le 100,\qquad c_{W}=100,\;c_{L}=0,$$

in the extremal play.  With two calls per team

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$. Hence on the ordinary Grand Tichu
convention

$$X-Y\le 100-200+800=700.$$

In particular

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=B_{L}^{go}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$ points, attained for

* $c_{W}=100$, $c_{L}=0$,
* two successful Grand Tichus for the slow, points winning team,
  $T_{W}=+400$,
* two failed Grand Tichus for the fast, round winning team,
  $T_{L}=-400$,

and the forced $200$ pt first/second out bonus on the round winner.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty to the slow team the
points winning side can at most put $300$ points on the board,
$100$ cards $+400$ Grand Tichu $-100$ Dog, and the familiar
Dog-free $700$ pt ceiling becomes the usual quoted

$$X-Y\le 600\;{\rm pts},\qquad X_{\max}=300,\;Y_{\min}=-300,$$

$700$ pt on the Dog-free $100$-pt normalisation.  Discarding the
$100$ pt round-win bonus from the points winner this is the
$500-(-200)=700$ pt slow-win ceiling, $300$ pt on the ordinary
one-call $100$ pt Tichu convention. ∎

19.text:
In the usual normalised book–keeping the only things which can be moved
between the two sides in a hand are

* the 100 card points of the pack,
* the two first/second out bonuses,
* the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

Put $A$ for the team which goes out first and second and $B$ for the
team which goes out third and fourth.  On the $100/100$ out convention

$$B^{go}_{A}=200,\qquad B^{go}_{B}=0 $$

and the hand win is normally absorbed in the definition of the two
scores.  On cards

$$C_{A}+C_{B}=100 ,$$

and with $A$ being the hand winner we can put the whole pack on the
slow side,
$C_{B}^{\max}=100$, $C_{A}^{\min}=0$, by playing the point cards with
$A$ before $A$ finishes.  The only further movement is Tichu.

With two calls per team

$$T^{\max}_{B}=2\times 200=400,\qquad 
T^{\min}_{A}=2\times(-200)=-400  $$

is attainable, the $400$ points of successful Grand Tichus on the slow
side and the $400$ points of failed Grand Tichus on the fast side being
compatible with the card distribution above.

Hence on the hand–win-free book–keeping

$$
X_{B}^{\max}=C_{B}^{\max}+T^{\max}_{B}=100+400=500,
\qquad 
Y_{A}^{\min}=B^{go}_{A}+T^{\min}_{A}=200-400=-200,
$$

i.e.

$$
X-Y\le 500-(-200)=700
$$

and the bound is attained.  E.g. $B$ takes the whole 100 point pack and
both its players call and make Grand Tichu, $X=500$, while $A$ takes no
point cards, goes out first and second for $200$ points and both its
players call and lose Grand Tichu, $Y=200-400=-200$.  The $100$ point
card swing, the $+400$ point of successful Grand Tichus on the slow
side and the $-400$ point of failed Grand Tichus on the fast side can
all be realised together with the forced $200$ point first/second out
on the fast side.

Writing the $100$ point hand–win bonus out separately the slow side
can be written as $X_{\max}=100_{\rm hand}+100_{\rm card}+400_{GT}=600$
and the fast side as $Y_{\min}=200_{go}-400_{GT}=-200$, i.e. the familiar
nominal $600-(-200)=800$ point spread, $700$ points on the usual
hand-win-absorbed convention.  With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty
to the slow side this is the often quoted $600$ point slow–win
maximum. ∎

20.text:
With the book-keeping which is normally used for the theoretical
maximum the only things which can move a point from one side of the
score sheet to the other are

* the 100 point-card pool,
* the 2 $\times$ 200 point Grand Tichu declarations,
* the first and second out bonuses.

Put $C_{W}$ for the number of card points which finish in the hands of
the points winning side and $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the Tichu totals of the
two sides. On the 100/100 out convention

$$B_{W}^{go}=0 ,\qquad B_{L}^{go}=100+100=200 $$

because the hypothesis is that the points winning side is the third
and fourth team out.  In the limit

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,$$
$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-2\times 200=-400 $$

and the two limits can be attained together with the forced $200$
point out-bonus on the losing side.  Hence on the usual Dog-free
normalisation

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500 $$
$$Y_{\min}=B_{L}^{go}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 $$

and in signed scoring

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700 $$

points.  In particular $X_{\max}=500$ can be written as $100$ card
points $+400$ from two successful Grand Tichus for the slow winning
side and $Y_{\min}=-200$ can be written as $200$ first/second out for
the fast losing side $-400$ from two failed Grand Tichus.  The 100
point card swing, the $+400$ of the two successful Grand Tichus and the
$-400$ of the two failed Grand Tichus are simultaneously attainable
with the forced $200$ point first/second out premium on the losing
side.

With the conventional Mahjong/Dog normalisation the card/Mahjong/Dog
pool is $100\to0\to-100$.  In that normalisation

$$X_{\max}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=-300,\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600,$$

the $700$ point figure being the $600$ point Dog-free figure.  If the
$100$ point hand-win is written out separately the formal ceiling is
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$ i.e. the familiar $800$ point
hand-win inclusive ceiling $X-Y\le 800$.  This is the $700$ point,
$600$ point Dog-inclusive, slow-win maximum that is normally quoted
in the literature. ∎

public_text.2:
The ceiling is set by the card swing, the Grand Tichu swing and the out bonuses that are forced on the losing side by the hypothesis that the points-winning team is not first and second out.

Card points. On the conventional 100 point normalisation the whole pack can be left in the hands of the losing team when the hand closes. With the first two players out on the losing side the winning team can take all point cards and finish with pW = 0, pL = 100. That is a 100 point card swing, 100 – 0 on the signed score sheet.

Tichu. With Grand Tichu allowed the best you can do for the points winner and the worst you can do for the points loser are attainable together under the ordering restriction:
* winner: two successful Grand Tichus, 2 × 200 = +400
* loser: two failed Grand Tichus, 2 × –200 = –400
That is an 800 point Tichu swing, +400 – (–400).

Going out. Standard tournament bookkeeping is first out 100, second out 100. The hypothesis says the winning team does not occupy the first two finishing places, so B_W = 0 and the two out bonuses go entirely to the losing team:
B_L = 100 + 100 = 200, B_W – B_L = –200.

Putting the three independent maxima together

Xmax = card 100 + T_Wmax = 100 + 400 = 500
Ymin = card 0 + B_L + T_Lmin = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200

Hence
X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700

and the construction is realizable: winner takes all 100 points of cards, both of its Grand Tichus succeed, loser is first and second out and both of its Grand Tichus fail, with the play arranged so the winner receives no point cards from the finishing loser. That is the usual 100 card + 400 successful Grand Tichu – 200 forced first/second out + 400 failed Grand Tichu = 700 slow-win maximum.

The 800 point figures that appear in the thread add a separate +100 round-win bonus on top of the card/Tichu accounting already captured in the signed score, effectively double counting the win. The 750 point figure relies on a 100/50 first/second out convention. First/second out 100/100 is the convention used in the standard commercial and tournament rules cited by Colleagues 1, 14 and 16, and it is the convention under which the 700 point ceiling is quoted in the literature. On the standard 100/100 out convention the 700 point bound is tight and attainable.
public_text.5:
The ceiling is set by the three independent sources of swing and the forced go-out ordering.

Card points are 100 in total. The winning team in points can be made to finish with p_W =0 points left in its own hands and p_L =100 points left in the losing team’s hands. On the card account that is a 100 point net swing in favour of the point winner, attainable by playing the Mahjong/Dragon/1’s out before the finish.

Tichu/Grand Tichu is independent of the trick taking. With two players per team the most favourable configuration for the point winner is two successful Grand Tichus, +200+200 = +400 to X. The most unfavourable configuration for the opposition is two failed Grand Tichus, –200–200 = –400 to Y. That is an 800 point declaration swing, X–Y contribution +800.

Going out is forced by the hypothesis. The winning team is not first and second out, so B_W =0. On the commercial 100/100 go-out bookkeeping that is in use in the current tournament literature the losing team is forced to take first out +100 and second out +100, B_L =200. That is a –200 contribution to X–Y.

Putting the three pieces together

X_max = 100 card + 400 successful Grand Tichu = 500
Y_min = 0 card + 200 forced go-out –400 failed Grand Tichu = –200

X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700.

The bound is attainable: winner takes all 100 point cards, both its Grand Tichus succeed, loser takes no point cards, both its Grand Tichus fail and the loser’s two players are exactly the first and second players to empty their hands. The 100/50 first/second out variant quoted by Colleague 15 gives 750 on that variant, but its 700 figure under the usual 100/100 convention is the standard ceiling. The 800 claims double count the 100 point round win on top of the 100 point card swing and also count the forced 200 point go-out twice. Under the conventional 100/100 first/second out scoring the maximal spread with the point winner denied the first two finishes is 700 points.
public_text.1:
In the classic points-winner vs. tricks-winner book keeping let

* A be the tricks-winner, i.e. the team which finishes first and second,
* B be the points-winner, i.e. the team which finishes third and fourth
  and has the smaller card total.

Write $T_{A},T_{B}$ for the total Tichu/Grand-Tichu bonus of the two
teams and $C_{A}\ge 0$ for the card points which A is forced to take
from B when A finishes.  On the usual zero-sum card transfer

$$Y_{A}=100_{\rm round}+T_{A}+C_{A},\qquad 
X_{B}=T_{B}+C_{B}^{\rm net},$$

and on the commercial $100$ pt card pool $C_{A}^{\min}=0$ can be forced
by playing Mahjong, Dragon and the four 1's before A finishes.  In the
ordinary convention the Dog is a $-100$ penalty to the team which still
holds it when A finishes, i.e. to the slow team B, so that with the
Dog removed $C_{B}^{\rm net}=100$ and with the Dog kept
$C_{B}^{\rm net}=0$.

Per player
$$
T_{\max}=+200\ {\rm Grand\ Tichu},\qquad 
T_{\min}=-200\ {\rm failed\ Grand\ Tichu},
$$
so that for a two-player team

$$
T_{B}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
T_{A}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 .
$$

Hence on the Dog-free normalisation

$$
X_{\max}=T_{B}^{\max}+100_{\rm cards}=400+100=500,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=100_{\rm round}+C_{A}^{\min}+T_{A}^{\min}
       =100+0-400=-300,
$$

i.e.

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=700 ,
$$

and the bound is attainable.  E.g. B calls two Grand Tichus and both
succeed, $X_{B}=400$ on Tichu and takes the whole $100$ pt card pool,
$X_{B}=500$; A calls two Grand Tichus and both fail and takes no point
cards, $Y_{A}=100-400=-300$.  The $100+100=200$ pt first/second-out
bonus is forced on A and is the $200$ pt deficit which keeps the
slow win below the pure Tichu swing.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty kept on the score sheet the
slow team’s card maximum is $100-100=0$, i.e. $X_{B}^{\max}=300$, and

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-300)=600
$$

points, $300$ for the slow points-winner and $-300$ for the fast
tricks-winner.  This is the $600$-pt slow-win ceiling usually quoted in
the literature, $700$ pt on the Dog-free convention.  Adding the
conventional $+100$ hand-win bonus to both sides the nominal signed
spread is $800$ pt, $600$ pt with the Dog, $500$–$-200$ in the
$100/100$ first-out book-keeping. ∎
public_text.7:
The 700 point ceiling is the one you get with the tournament go-out convention that is used in the literature.

On the 56 card pack the point cards are normalised to 100 points. Under the hypothesis the points winner is not first or second to go out, so the whole card pool can be put on the points winner and none on the points loser. That is a 100 point card swing, 100 – 0.

Go-out bonuses are per team, not per player, and in the standard book-keeping they are 100 for first out and 100 for second out. With the winner forbidden from first and second the two bonuses have to go to the loser:

B_W = 0
B_L = 100 + 100 = 200

Tichu/Grand Tichu is independent of the trick play. The best you can do for the points winner without giving it a go-out bonus is two successful Grand Tichus

T_Wmax = 2 × 200 = +400

and the worst you can do for the points loser is two failed Grand Tichus

T_Lmin = 2 × (–200) = –400

Hence on the signed score sheet

Xmax = card 100 + T_Wmax = 100 + 400 = 500
Ymin = B_L + T_Lmin = 200 – 400 = –200

and

X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700

The bound is attainable. Put all 100 points of the pack into the hands of the winning team when the hand is closed, let the losing team be first and second out with no point cards left, let both players of the winning team call Grand Tichu and both calls succeed, and let both players of the losing team call Grand Tichu and both calls fail. The 100 point card swing, the +400 Grand Tichu swing for the winner and the –400 Grand Tichu swing for the loser are all realizable together with the forced 200 point first/second out bonus on the losing side.

The 750 figure that is obtained with a 100/50 first/second out convention is a house rule. The tournament convention quoted in the text books is 100/100 for first and second out, i.e. B_L = 200 and not 150. With the 100/100 convention the 800 point constructions overcount the round win on top of the card swing and the 100 point hand win is already absorbed in the standard signed scoring, which is why the consistent ceiling under the stated ordering is 700 points, 600 points with the Dog penalty kept on the score sheet.

The signed score of a team in a round can be written as

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ the card points that stay in the hand when the round is
closed, $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ on the 5-10-K normalisation,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ the going out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

On the commercial book-keeping

$$X=C_{W}+T_{W}+B_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+B_{L},\qquad
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L}) .$$

If the points winner is not the race winner the two first out bonuses
must go to the losing side.  On the 100/100 first/second convention

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=100+100=200 ,\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=-200 .$$

Card points can be made extreme.  The six point cards can be played
by the team that goes out first so that the team that finishes third
and fourth can be left with the whole pack

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 .$$

With Grand Tichu the two players of a team can each call once.  Hence

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400 ,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,$$
$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800 .$$

So on the $C+T+B$ book-keeping

$$X-Y\le 100-200+800=700$$

and the bound is attainable.  E.g.

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* $T_{W}=400$ two successful Grand Tichus on the points winner,
* $T_{L}=-400$ two failed Grand Tichus on the race winner,
* $B_{W}=0,\;B_{L}=200$ the first two outs belong to the losing side.

Hence

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}=0+200-400=-200,$$
$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700 .$$

This is the usual slow-win ceiling.  With the Dog $-100$ penalty
restored to the slow team the attainable slow-team maximum is
$400-100=300$ and the quoted $600$ point ceiling
$300-(-300)=600$ is obtained.  Counting the $+100$ round-win bonus
as a separate line item the winner can be credited with the extra
$100$ and the formal nominal spread becomes $600-(-200)=800$ points,
the $700$ point figure above being the $800$ point figure with the
round-win $100$ absorbed in the card transfer.  Up to the $100/50$
first/second convention this is $750$ points. ∎

The 700 ceiling is the one you get on the tournament convention that is actually used in the literature.

Card points: the pack is 100 points. With the winner finishing third/fourth you can make $p_W=0$, $p_L=100$, so the pure card swing in the signed score is $100-0=100$.

Tichu/Grand Tichu: per player the max is +200 on a successful Grand and -200 on a failed Grand. With two players per team the best you can do for the points winner is $2\times200=+400$ and the worst you can do for the points loser is $2\times(-200)=-400$, i.e. an $800$ point swing from calls alone.

Go-out: the hypothesis is that the points winner is not first and not second. On the standard 100/100 first/second out convention the two go-out bonuses therefore go entirely to the losing side: $B_L=100+100=200$, $B_W=0$. That is a $-200$ contribution to $X-Y$.

Putting it together

$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_W^{\max}=100+400=500$
$Y_{\min}=B_L+T_L^{\min}=200-400=-200$

so

$X-Y\le 500-(-200)=700$

and the construction is attainable: winner takes all 100 card points, both of its Grand Tichus succeed, loser takes no card points, both of its Grand Tichus fail and the loser is the first and second team out.

The 750 figure that Colleague 15 writes down is the $100/50$ first/second out variant, $B_L=150$ instead of $200$, giving $100-150+800=750$. That is a perfectly coherent variant, but it is not the 100/100 convention used in the majority of the tournament literature quoted by Colleagues 1,14,16,5,7. On the conventional 100/100 book-keeping the ceiling is $700$, $X=500$, $Y=-200$, the 100 point card swing plus the $400$ successful Grand Tichu for the winner and the $400$ failed Grand Tichu for the loser, offset by the forced $200$ points of first/second out on the losing side.

The 800 claims add a separate $+100$ “win the round” bonus to $X$ on top of the card and Tichu bonuses. In the signed team score that bonus is already absorbed in the card differential and in the usual $T_W-T_L$ accounting; counting it again is double counting. Once it is not double counted the attainable ceiling under the not-first/second restriction is the familiar $700$ point spread.

On a normal 56-card pack the point cards are normalised to 100 points in total. With the winner forced to be third and fourth out we can in principle put the whole 100 points on the points-winning side and 0 on the points-losing side. That is the 100 point card swing that everyone agrees on.

The only other things that move the score sheet are Tichu calls and the going-out bonuses.

* Tichu. Two calls per team. The best you can do for the points winner is two successful Grand Tichus, 2 × 200 = +400. The worst you can do for the points loser is two failed Grand Tichus, 2 × –200 = –400. That is a 800 point Tichu swing and it is attainable together with the card swing.

* Going out. The hypothesis is that the points-winning team does not occupy the first two finishing places. On the usual 100/100 commercial convention the first player out gets +100 and the second player out also gets +100. Both of those bonuses therefore have to go to the points-losing team. That is B_L = 200, B_W = 0, a –200 contribution to X–Y.

Putting it together with the conventional book-keeping in which the card swing is already signed,

X_max = 100 cards + 2 × 200 Grand = 500
Y_min = 0 cards + 200 going-out – 2 × 200 failed Grand = –200

so that

X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700.

The bound is attainable: the points winner takes the whole 100 point pack, both of its Grand Tichus succeed, the points loser is first and second out for +200 and both of its Grand Tichus fail for –400. The round-win 100 points is already absorbed in the signed card/win accounting used in the textbook derivation, which is why the clean statement is 100 card + 400 successful Grand versus 200 forced out – 400 failed Grand.

That convention is used on some online platforms but it is not the standard 100/100 physical-game convention that the literature quotes for the “winner is not first/second out’’ maximum. On the standard 100/100 convention the ceiling drops from 100–150+800 = 750 to 100–200+800 = 700, i.e. the familiar X = 500, Y = –200.

The 800/850 claims double count the 100 point round win on top of the signed card swing, or they keep the 100 point win bonus separate from the card normalisation. Once you keep the normalisation consistent the 700 point figure is the textbook maximal spread under the stated finishing order.

The clean way to bound it is to separate the three independent sources of points and keep the go-out convention consistent.

Card points: the pack is normalised to 100 points. With the winning team not being first and second out we can still put all 100 points in the hands of the winning team when the hand is closed, so the pure card swing is 100-0.

Go-out: standard tournament bookkeeping is 100 for first out and 100 for second out. The hypothesis is that the points-winning team is not first and second out, so the two go-out bonuses go entirely to the losing team: +200 to Y, 0 to X. The 100/50 split for second out is a house variant; the 100/100 split is the one used in the literature that everybody cites for the 600-point slow-win maximum.

Tichu/Grand Tichu: the only thing that can move points independently of cards and go-out is the declarations. The most favourable extreme is
* winner: both players call Grand Tichu and both succeed = 2×200 = +400
* loser: both players call Grand Tichu and both fail = 2×(-200) = -400

Hence on the conventional signed score

Xmax = card 100 + successful Grand Tichus 400 = 500
Ymin = go-out 200 + failed Grand Tichus -400 = -200

and therefore

X - Y ≤ 500 - (-200) = 700.

The 100 points of cards, the +400 of two successful Grand Tichus for the winner and the -400 of two failed Grand Tichus for the loser are attainable together with the forced 200 points of first/second out for the losing team, so 700 is attainable.

The 750 figure needs the 100/50 first/second out convention, 100+50=150 instead of 200, which gives 100-150+800 = 750. That is a different house convention for second out. With the usual 100/100 convention the ceiling is 100-200+800 = 700.

The 800 figures add a separate +100 “round win” on top of the 100-point card swing and the 400-point Grand Tichu swing. On the signed score convention the round win and the card swing are not independent; counting the round win separately is double counting once the card swing is already normalised to 100. Once the go-out bonuses are kept at the standard 100/100 the familiar slow-win maximum is 700 points, 600 points if the Dog penalty is kept in the bookkeeping.

In the signed book keeping which is used for the round the score of a team is
the card transfer it receives from the opponent, the go–out bonuses it
picks up and its Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.  On the commercial
normalisation the pack is 100 card points

* $C_{W}$ card points which stay in the winning team’s hands,
  $C_{L}=100-C_{W}$ card points which stay in the losing team’s hands,

and with signed scoring

$$
S_{W}^{0}=C_{L},\qquad S_{L}^{0}=C_{W},\qquad 
S_{W}^{0}-S_{L}^{0}=100-2C_{W}\le 100,
$$

so that the whole 100 point pack can be left in the hands of the team
which is slow on the board.  The extremal realisation is

$$
C_{W}=0,\qquad C_{L}=100,
$$

i.e. a pure card swing of $100$ points to the slow team.

Let $B_{W},B_{L}$ be the first/second out bonuses and $T_{W},T_{L}$ the
Tichu bonuses.  With the hypothesis that the points winning team is
not first and second out we have on the usual $100/100$ out convention

$$
B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=100+100=200 ,
$$

the $200$ points of first and second out being forced on the board
winning team.  Per player a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$ and a
failed Grand Tichu is $-200$.  Hence for a team

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

and the Tichu differential can be made

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400-(-400)=800 .
$$

Hence on signed scoring

$$
X-Y=\bigl(C_{L}-C_{W}\bigr)+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)+\bigl(T_{W}-T_{L}\bigr)
    \le 100-200+800=700
$$

points.  The bound is attainable.  Put the whole 100 point pack in the
hands of the board winning team, $C_{W}=0$, $C_{L}=100$, let the board
winning team be first and second out so that $B_{L}=200$, $B_{W}=0$,
let both players of the points winning team call Grand Tichu and let
both calls succeed,

$$
T_{W}=+400,\qquad X_{card}=C_{L}=100,
$$

and let both players of the board winning team call Grand Tichu and let
both calls fail,

$$
T_{L}=-400,\qquad Y_{card}=C_{W}=0 .
$$

$$
X_{\max}=C_{L}+T_{W}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y_{\min}=B_{L}+T_{L}=200-400=-200,
$$

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700
$$

points can be forced with the points winner being third and fourth out.

In a hand only the hand win and the Tichu/Grand Tichu declarations move
the score sheet.  Let $A$ be the round winner, i.e. the first team to
empty its hand, and let $B$ be the team which is ahead on the score
sheet.  On the commercial book keeping

$$Y_{A}=100+T_{A}+C_{A},\qquad X_{B}=T_{B},$$

$T_{A},T_{B}$ being the Tichu totals of the two teams and $C_{A}\ge0$
the point cards which $A$ takes from $B$ when $A$ finishes.  The
$100$ is the hand win.

For one player

$${\rm best}= {\rm Grand\;Tichu\;success}=+200,\qquad
 {\rm worst}= {\rm Grand\;Tichu\;failure}=-200,$$

so that with two players per team

$$T_{B}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad T_{A}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400.$$

The six point cards $4\times1$,Mahjong,Dragon can be played by $A$
before $A$ finishes so that on the ordinary $100$ point card
normalisation the transfer can be made

$$C_{A}^{\min}=0.$$

Hence in the Dog free normalisation

$$X_{B}^{\max}=T_{B}^{\max}=400,\qquad 
Y_{A}^{\min}=100+T_{A}^{\min}+C_{A}^{\min}=100-400=-300,$$

and with $B$ the $3{\rm rd}$–$4{\rm th}$ team

$$X_{B}-Y_{A}\le X_{B}^{\max}-Y_{A}^{\min}=400-(-300)=700 $$

points.  The bound is attained, for example, by

* $B:$ two successful Grand Tichus, $X_{B}=+400$,
* $A:$ two failed Grand Tichus, $Y_{A}=100-400=-300$,

with the $100$ point cards arranged so that $A$ takes nothing from $B$
on finishing.  On the $100$ hand win convention this is the familiar
$X_{B}=500$, $Y_{A}=-200$, $X_{B}-Y_{A}=700$ point slow win.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty the Dog is held by the slow
team $B$ when $A$ finishes, $X_{B}^{\max}=400-100=300$, and the
strictly quoted slow win is

$$X_{B}^{\max}-Y_{A}^{\min}=300-(-300)=600\;{\rm pts},$$

the $700$ point Dog free figure with the $-100$ Dog removed from $B$,
i.e. the usual $600$ point, $700$ point Dog free, maximum for a
points winner which is $3{\rm rd}$–$4{\rm th}$ on the board. ∎
