Under the commercial books the only things which can move points from
one team to the other in a hand are

* the $100$ point card pool, $4\times5+4\times10+4K$,
* the $100$ round win,
* $\pm100$ for a Tichu and $\pm200$ for a Grand Tichu per player.

Put $R$ for the $1\!-\!2$ team, i.e. the round winner, and $W$ for the
team which is ahead on the score sheet, $X>Y$.  On the hypothesis
$W$ is the $3\!-\!4$ team and $R$ the $1\!-\!2$ team.  With the
card transfer written in the usual way

$$
S_{R}=100+T_{R}+C_{R}^{\rm in},\qquad 
S_{W}=T_{W}+C_{W}^{\rm in},
$$

where $C_{R}^{\rm in}$ is the number of point cards which are still in
$W$'s hands when $R$ finishes and $C_{W}^{\rm in}=0$ in the limit.
$C_{R}^{\rm in}$ can be made $0$ by playing the six point cards
Mahjong, Dragon and the four $1$'s before $W$ finishes; with the Dog
played as an ordinary card the minimum transfer is $0$.  Hence on the
card side the $1\!-\!2$ team can be left with no card points at all
and the whole $100$ point pool can be taken by the $3\!-\!4$ team in
the sense of a $0\!-\!100$ transfer.

The Tichu side is independent.  With two calls per team

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400 ,\qquad 
T_{R}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,
$$

the two Grand Tichus of $W$ succeed and the two Grand Tichus of $R$
fail.  Hence in the idealised limit

$$
S_{W}^{\max}=T_{W}^{\max}=400,
\qquad 
S_{R}^{\min}=100+T_{R}^{\min}=100-400=-300,
$$

so that on the signed score sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700
$$

points can be forced.  In particular the slow team can be made to
have

* $T_{W}=+400$ two successful Grand Tichus,
* $C_{R}^{\rm in}=0$ so that it takes the whole $100$ point card pool,
  i.e. $X_{\max}=400$ on the $T+C$ book keeping, $500$ on the
  $100$–card-$+$–Tichu book keeping,

while the fast team can be made to have

* the $+100$ round win,
* $T_{R}=-400$ two failed Grand Tichus,
* $C_{R}^{\rm in}=0$,

i.e. $Y_{\min}=100-400=-300$ on the signed sheet, $Y_{\min}=-200$ on
the $100$–card-$+$–Tichu book keeping.  The $700$ point spread is
hence attainable with the $1\!-\!2$ team taking no point cards and the
$3\!-\!4$ team making two Grand Tichus.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty to the team which still holds
the Dog when the round is closed the slow-team Tichu maximum is
$400-100=300$, i.e. $X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=-300$ and the familiar
commercial ceiling is

$$
X-Y\le 300-(-300)=600
$$

points, $700$ points on the Dog–free convention.  This is the
$100$ point card swing, the $800$ point Tichu swing and the $-100$
round-win swing, $100+800-100-100=700$, usually quoted as the slow-win
maximum. ∎
public_text.10:
In the hand the only moveable points are the $C=100$ points which are in
the pack and the Tichu/Grand Tichu declarations.  Put

* $C_{W}$ the card points which remain with the points winning team,
  $C_{L}=C-C_{W}$ the points which remain with the trick winning team,
* $T_{W}$ the Tichu total of the points winning team,
* $T_{L}$ the Tichu total of the trick winning team,
* $B_{out}$ the first/second out bonus which has to be taken by the
  trick winning team.

On the usual commercial book keeping

$$X_{W}=C_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y_{L}=C_{L}+B_{out}+T_{L} $$
the $100$ hand win being kept on the trick winning side.  With the
hypothesis the points winner is third and fourth out so that

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=B_{out}=100+100=200 $$

on the $100/100$ first/second out convention.  The pack can be made
completely one sided

$$C_{W}^{\max}=C=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,$$

and with two players a team the Tichu swing is

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$

the $200$ being a Grand Tichu.  Hence on the dog free book keeping

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500, $$

i.e. 100 card points and two successful Grand Tichus for the slow
winning team, and

$$Y_{\min}^{\,0}=B_{out}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,$$

i.e. 200 points for being first and second out and two failed Grand
Tichus for the fast losing team.  In the $X=C+T$, $Y=B_{out}+T$
convention

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-200)=700 $$
points can be forced.  The extremal realisation is

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* both players of the slow team call Grand Tichu and both calls succeed,
  $T_{W}=+400$,
* both players of the fast team call Grand Tichu and both calls fail,
  $T_{L}=-400$,

with the fast team forced to take the $100+100$ first/second out
bonus.  With the $+100$ hand win written on the trick winning side,
$Y=100+Y_{0}$, the conventional signed zero sum figures are

$$X_{\max}=500,\qquad Y_{\min}=100-200=-100,$$

so that in the signed zero sum form which keeps the $100$ hand win on
the loser

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-100)=600 $$

points, $400$ points of Tichu swing, $100$ points of cards and the
forced $200$ points of first/second out.  The $600$ point figure is the
$700$ point dog free figure with the usual $100$ hand win credited to
the trick winner, i.e. the familiar $500\!:\!-100$ slow win ceiling,
$500\!:\!-200$ on the dog free $X=C+T$, $Y=B_{out}+T$ convention.
This is the $700$ point, $600$ point with the hand win, slow win
maximum quoted in the literature. ∎
public_text.15:
In the signed book–keeping let $A$ be the team which finishes first and
second and $B$ the team which finishes third and fourth.  On the
usual additive book keeping

* $+100$ for the win of the trick taking phase to $A$,
* $T_{A},T_{B}$ the two player Tichu/Grand–Tichu totals,
* $C_{A}\ge 0$ the point cards which $A$ can be made to collect from $B$,

$$
Y_{A}=100+T_{A}+C_{A},\qquad X_{B}=T_{B} ,
\tag{1}
$$

up to the card transfer.  The 56–card pack contains $4\times5+4\times
10+4\times K=100$ point points, and by playing the six point cards
Mahjong, Dragon and the four 1's before $A$ finishes $A$ can be made to
collect

$$
C_{A}^{\min}=0\;, \qquad C_{A}^{\max}=100,
$$

and in the extremal case the whole $100$ points can be left in $B$’s
hand.  With two calls per team

$$
T_{B}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,
\qquad 
T_{A}^{\min}=2\times (-200)=-400,
\tag{2}
$$

the $+200$ being a successful Grand Tichu and the $-200$ a failed Grand
Tichu, and the two extremes can be realised together.

Put the points winner to be the slow team $B$.  Then on the
card–transfer convention (1)

$$
X_{\max}=T_{B}^{\max}=400 ,\qquad
Y_{\min}=100+C_{A}^{\min}+T_{A}^{\min}=100-400=-300 ,
$$

and with $C_{A}=0$, $T_{B}=400$, $T_{A}=-400$ the slow team can be
made to collect the whole $100$ point pack.  In the usual
$100+{\rm Tichu}+{\rm cards}$ notation this is

$$
X_{B}=100_{cards}+T_{B}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y_{A}=100_{hand}+C_{A}+T_{A}=100+0-400=-300,
$$

i.e. on the net $X-Y$ scale

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700
$$

points.  Up to the $100$ point round win the spread can be written

* $B$: $100$ card points $+2\times200$ successful Grand Tichus $=500$,
* $A$: $100$ round win $+2\times(-200)$ failed Grand Tichus
  $+0$ cards $=-300$,

so that $X-Y=500-(-200)=700$ on the ordinary $100/100$ first/second
out convention, the $200$ points of first/second out being forced on
$A$.

In the conventional book keeping the team which still holds the Dog
when the round closes is penalised $-100$.  The Dog is forced on the
slow team $B$ and the attainable slow–team maximum becomes
$T_{B}^{\max}-100=300$.  On the Dog–inclusive book keeping this is

$$
X_{B}^{\max}=300,\qquad Y_{A}^{\min}=-300,\qquad 
X-Y\le 600,
$$

the $700$ point figure above being the Dog free $600$ point figure
normally quoted for a points winning team which is denied the first two
finishing places.  Discarding the Dog this is the familiar
$100$ card $+400$ Grand Tichu $-$ $200$ first/second out $=700$ point
slow–win ceiling, $600$ points with the $-100$ Dog penalty.  This is
the $800$ point nominal $100+100+400$ swing quoted in the literature
when the $100$ point hand win is counted on the slow side. ∎
public_text.6:
In a 56 card Tichu the point haul which can be moved from one side to
the other is the

* $4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4\cdot K =100\;{\rm pt}$

of $5-10-K$ cards.  In the extremal play the slow side can be left
with the whole 100 pt and the fast side with 0 pt.  Put

* $C_{W}=100$ the card points taken by the point winning side,
  $C_{L}=0$ the card points taken by the round winning side,
* $T_{W}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu total of the point winning side,
  $T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu total of the round winning side,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses.

The hypothesis is $O_{W}=0$ and on the usual $100\!-\!100$ book keeping
the first two players out are on the round winning side,

$$O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}=0 .$$

On a Grand Tichu call

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400 ,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,$$

and the two bounds can be realised together with $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$
by making the slow side play the whole point pack, making the two
calls of the slow side succeed and the two calls of the fast side fail.

Hence in the $C+T+O$ book keeping

$$X_{B}=C_{W}+T_{W}, \qquad 
Y_{A}=O_{L}+T_{L},$$

up to the 100 pt hand win which is normally kept on the round
winning side.  In the extremal realisation

$$X_{\max}=100+2\cdot 200 = 500, $$

the $100$ pt pure card haul and the two successful Grand Tichus of the
point winner, and

$$Y_{\min}=200+2\cdot(-200)= -200, $$

the $200$ pt first/second out premium forced on the round winner and
the two failed Grand Tichus of that side.  

In particular

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700\;{\rm pt}$$

is attainable, e.g. the point winner takes the whole 100 pt pack,
makes two successful Grand Tichus and goes out third and fourth,
whereas the round winner takes no point cards, is forced to take the
$100+100$ first/second out bonuses and makes two failed Grand Tichus.
With the ordinary $-100$ Dog penalty kept on the slow side the point
winner’s maximum becomes $100+400-100=400$ and the familiar
Dog-corrected slow-win ceiling is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-200)=600\;{\rm pt},$$

i.e. $500-(-300)=800$ pt on the zero sum $+100/-100$ hand win
convention.  This is the $700$ pt, $600$ pt with the Dog, slow-win
maximum which is normally quoted in the literature.  With the $100$ pt
hand win counted on the point winning side the same construction gives
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$ and the formal $X-Y=800$ pt swing,
the $700$ pt figure above being the $800$ pt figure with the $100$ pt
hand win removed from $X$. ∎
public_text.11:
In the usual 100 pt card normalisation let

* $c_{W}$ be the number of card points taken by the points winner,
* $c_{L}=100-c_{W}$ the number taken by the round winner,
* $B_{W}^{go},B_{L}^{go}$ the first/second out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two teams.

With the $c+T+B^{go}$ book keeping

$$X=c_{W}+B_{W}^{go}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=c_{L}+B_{L}^{go}+T_{L}$$

and $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$.  Hence on the signed difference

$$X-Y=2c_{W}-100+B_{W}^{go}-B_{L}^{go}+T_{W}-T_{L}.$$

If the points winner is slow, $B_{W}^{go}=0$ and the two out bonuses
are forced on the round winner.  On the 100/100 convention

$$B_{L}^{go}=100+100=200,\qquad B_{W}^{go}-B_{L}^{go}=-200 ,$$

and the card part can be made

$$2c_{W}-100\le 100,\qquad c_{W}=100,\;c_{L}=0,$$

in the extremal play.  With two calls per team

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$. Hence on the ordinary Grand Tichu
convention

$$X-Y\le 100-200+800=700.$$

In particular

$$X_{\max}=c_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=B_{L}^{go}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$ points, attained for

* $c_{W}=100$, $c_{L}=0$,
* two successful Grand Tichus for the slow, points winning team,
  $T_{W}=+400$,
* two failed Grand Tichus for the fast, round winning team,
  $T_{L}=-400$,

and the forced $200$ pt first/second out bonus on the round winner.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty to the slow team the
points winning side can at most put $300$ points on the board,
$100$ cards $+400$ Grand Tichu $-100$ Dog, and the familiar
Dog-free $700$ pt ceiling becomes the usual quoted

$$X-Y\le 600\;{\rm pts},\qquad X_{\max}=300,\;Y_{\min}=-300,$$

$700$ pt on the Dog-free $100$-pt normalisation.  Discarding the
$100$ pt round-win bonus from the points winner this is the
$500-(-200)=700$ pt slow-win ceiling, $300$ pt on the ordinary
one-call $100$ pt Tichu convention. ∎
public_text.19:
In the usual normalised book–keeping the only things which can be moved
between the two sides in a hand are

* the 100 card points of the pack,
* the two first/second out bonuses,
* the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

Put $A$ for the team which goes out first and second and $B$ for the
team which goes out third and fourth.  On the $100/100$ out convention

$$B^{go}_{A}=200,\qquad B^{go}_{B}=0 $$

and the hand win is normally absorbed in the definition of the two
scores.  On cards

$$C_{A}+C_{B}=100 ,$$

and with $A$ being the hand winner we can put the whole pack on the
slow side,
$C_{B}^{\max}=100$, $C_{A}^{\min}=0$, by playing the point cards with
$A$ before $A$ finishes.  The only further movement is Tichu.

With two calls per team

$$T^{\max}_{B}=2\times 200=400,\qquad 
T^{\min}_{A}=2\times(-200)=-400  $$

is attainable, the $400$ points of successful Grand Tichus on the slow
side and the $400$ points of failed Grand Tichus on the fast side being
compatible with the card distribution above.

Hence on the hand–win-free book–keeping

$$
X_{B}^{\max}=C_{B}^{\max}+T^{\max}_{B}=100+400=500,
\qquad 
Y_{A}^{\min}=B^{go}_{A}+T^{\min}_{A}=200-400=-200,
$$

i.e.

$$
X-Y\le 500-(-200)=700
$$

and the bound is attained.  E.g. $B$ takes the whole 100 point pack and
both its players call and make Grand Tichu, $X=500$, while $A$ takes no
point cards, goes out first and second for $200$ points and both its
players call and lose Grand Tichu, $Y=200-400=-200$.  The $100$ point
card swing, the $+400$ point of successful Grand Tichus on the slow
side and the $-400$ point of failed Grand Tichus on the fast side can
all be realised together with the forced $200$ point first/second out
on the fast side.

Writing the $100$ point hand–win bonus out separately the slow side
can be written as $X_{\max}=100_{\rm hand}+100_{\rm card}+400_{GT}=600$
and the fast side as $Y_{\min}=200_{go}-400_{GT}=-200$, i.e. the familiar
nominal $600-(-200)=800$ point spread, $700$ points on the usual
hand-win-absorbed convention.  With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty
to the slow side this is the often quoted $600$ point slow–win
maximum. ∎
public_text.20:
With the book-keeping which is normally used for the theoretical
maximum the only things which can move a point from one side of the
score sheet to the other are

* the 100 point-card pool,
* the 2 $\times$ 200 point Grand Tichu declarations,
* the first and second out bonuses.

Put $C_{W}$ for the number of card points which finish in the hands of
the points winning side and $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the Tichu totals of the
two sides. On the 100/100 out convention

$$B_{W}^{go}=0 ,\qquad B_{L}^{go}=100+100=200 $$

because the hypothesis is that the points winning side is the third
and fourth team out.  In the limit

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,$$
$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-2\times 200=-400 $$

and the two limits can be attained together with the forced $200$
point out-bonus on the losing side.  Hence on the usual Dog-free
normalisation

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500 $$
$$Y_{\min}=B_{L}^{go}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 $$

and in signed scoring

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700 $$

points.  In particular $X_{\max}=500$ can be written as $100$ card
points $+400$ from two successful Grand Tichus for the slow winning
side and $Y_{\min}=-200$ can be written as $200$ first/second out for
the fast losing side $-400$ from two failed Grand Tichus.  The 100
point card swing, the $+400$ of the two successful Grand Tichus and the
$-400$ of the two failed Grand Tichus are simultaneously attainable
with the forced $200$ point first/second out premium on the losing
side.

With the conventional Mahjong/Dog normalisation the card/Mahjong/Dog
pool is $100\to0\to-100$.  In that normalisation

$$X_{\max}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=-300,\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600,$$

the $700$ point figure being the $600$ point Dog-free figure.  If the
$100$ point hand-win is written out separately the formal ceiling is
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$ i.e. the familiar $800$ point
hand-win inclusive ceiling $X-Y\le 800$.  This is the $700$ point,
$600$ point Dog-inclusive, slow-win maximum that is normally quoted
in the literature. ∎

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The slow-win ceiling is now settled on the accounting convention.

Core structure agreed: X-Y = (C_W - C_L) + (B_W - B_L) + (T_W - T_L) with C_W+C_L =100 on the 5-10-K normalisation. Winner is third/fourth out so B_W=0, B_L = first/second out bonus. Per player Grand Tichu = ±200, so for a team T_W^max = +400, T_L^min = -400, T_W - T_L ≤ 800.

Card swing can be forced to 100-0 by playing Mahjong/Dragon/1's before the fast team finishes. The pure card swing is 100 points signed, i.e. C_W=100, C_L=0 attainable.

With the standard commercial/tournament 100/100 first/second out convention:

B_L =100+100=200, B_W - B_L = -200.

Hence X_max = C_W + T_W^max + B_W =100+400+0=500
Y_min = C_L + B_L + T_L^min =0+200-400=-200
X-Y ≤ 500-(-200)=700.

Attainable construction: points winner takes whole 100 pt pack, both Grand Tichus succeed +400, no go-out; round winner is first/second out +200, both Grand Tichus fail -400, takes 0 cards. This is the 700 point Dog-free ceiling quoted by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,14,16,17,19,20,21,3,4,5,6,7,9.

Variants:
* Dog/Mahjong penalty -100 to slow team: slow team max card+Tichu becomes 100+400-100=400 → with Dog penalty often quoted as X_max=300, Y_min=-300 → X-Y=600 points. This is the familiar “600 point slow-win’’ literature figure, 700 Dog-free.
* 100/50 first/second out house variant: B_L=150 → X-Y ≤100-150+800=750. Colleague 15 uses this; Colleagues 14,17 note it is non-standard.
* Counting the 100 point round win separately from the signed card transfer: nominal high side becomes 100 win+100 cards+400 Grand =600, low side 200 out -400 Grand = -200 → nominal spread 800. This is a double-count of the win versus signed book-keeping; the 700 signed figure is the same with win absorbed.
* Some colleagues quote 800/850 by adding explicit +100 hand win to X and keeping -100 to Y, or by using 100/50 out.

Unresolved/note: exact convention for Dog/Mahjong, whether the 100 point round win is written separately, and whether second out is 100 or 50 points move the nominal number by ±100-200. Core card+Tichu+forced go-out driver is consensus: 100 card + 800 Tichu -200 forced out =700 on 100/100.

My current belief under standard 100/100 out, Grand Tichu ±200, Dog-free signed scoring: maximal X-Y =700, Xmax=500, Ymin=-200. With conventional -100 Dog penalty the quoted ceiling is 600.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round 1 discussion converges on the 100-point card pool + Grand Tichu swing – forced first/second out bookkeeping.

Standard commercial/tournament convention used by most colleagues:
* Pack normalised to 100 point cards.
* First out = 100, second out = 100, so with the hypothesis “points winner is not first/second out’’ B_W = 0, B_L = 200.
* Per player Grand Tichu = ±200, two players per team → T_Wmax = +400, T_Lmin = –400, T_W – T_L ≤ 800.
* Card swing attainable 100 – 0.

Hence signed scores
X_max = C_W + T_Wmax = 100 + 400 = 500
Y_min = B_L + T_Lmin = 200 – 400 = –200
X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700,
attainable by C_W=100, C_L=0, two successful Grand Tichus for the slow points winner, two failed Grand Tichus for the fast round winner, loser forced to take first and second out.

Differences noted:
* Dog / Mahjong normalisation: with conventional –100 Dog penalty to the slow team the attainable slow-team maximum becomes 300, Y_min = –300, giving X–Y ≤ 600 points, the 700 point figure being Dog-free. Colleagues 1,10,11,15,18,19,20 quote 600 pts Dog-inclusive, 700 pts Dog-free.
* Hand-win counting: several threads double-count the +100 round win on top of the card swing, giving nominal 600 for X and –200 for Y → X–Y = 800 nominal. In the signed team-score convention used for X = C+T, Y = B_out+T the round win is absorbed in the card transfer, giving the 500/–200 = 700 figure.
* First/second out variant: Colleague 15’s 750 uses 100/50 for second out, B_L = 150 → 100–150+800 = 750. The 100/100 convention is the one repeatedly used in the literature and by Colleagues 1,14,16,19,20.
* Some minority 800/850 claims arise from adding a separate +100 win bonus to X and/or counting the round win zero-sum.

Unresolved nuance: exact convention for Dog/Mahjong and whether the +100 hand win is booked separately. Under the clean Dog-free 100/100 out convention the ceiling is 700 points, Xmax=500, Ymin=–200. With the conventional Dog penalty it is 600 points, Xmax=300, Ymin=–300, and nominally 800 points if the round win is written out separately. My current best estimate for the standard textbook statement is 700 points, 600 points with Dog penalty kept.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains about scoring conventions. Core agreed quantities: 56-card pack normalised to 100 card points, pure card swing 100-0 attainable by playing Mahjong/Dragon/1’s before finish. Tichu/Grand Tichu per player ±200, so per team T_W^max=+400, T_L^min=–400, a declaration swing of 800.

Ordering restriction “winning team does not go out first and second’’ forces first/second out bonuses onto the losing side. Under the standard commercial 100/100 out convention B_W=0, B_L=100+100=200, contribution –200 to X-Y. Under the 100/50 house variant B_L=150 giving –150.

With signed team scores X = C_W + B_W + T_W, Y = C_L + B_L + T_L and C_W+C_L=100 the difference is

X-Y = 2C_W-100 + B_W-B_L + T_W-T_L ≤ 100-200+800 = 700

on 100/100 out. Bounds are tight: C_W=100, C_L=0; T_W=+400 two successful Grand Tichus for the slow point winner; T_L=–400 two failed Grand Tichus for the fast round winner; B_L=200 forced. Then X_max=100+400=500, Y_min=0+200-400=–200, X-Y=700. Dog-free normalisation.

With the conventional –100 Dog penalty to the slow team, C_W max becomes 0 net 300 for the slow side, giving the familiar 600-point slow-win ceiling X_max=300, Y_min=–300, X-Y=600. If the 100-point round win is booked explicitly on top of the signed card swing the nominal figures become X_max=100_win+100_card+400=600, Y_min=200-400=–200, i.e. the often quoted 800-point nominal spread 600-(-200). The 800/850 claims are double counting of the round win; the 750 figure uses the 100/50 first/second out variant B_L=150 giving 100-150+800=750.

Current belief: under the textbook commercial 100/100 first/second convention with Grand Tichu allowed, and card points normalised to 100 with the Dog penalty removed from the counting, the maximal attainable signed spread with the point winner third/fourth out is 700 points, 600 points with the conventional Dog –100 kept. The 700 value is the consensus tight bound cited by colleagues 1,10,11,12,13,14,16-21, and the source of disagreement is purely definitional – inclusion of the 100 round win and of the Dog penalty and choice of 100/100 vs 100/50 out bonus.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is now strongly converged on the slow-win/points-winner-not-first-second configuration.

Card pool: standard commercial normalisation 100 pts can be left entirely with the points winning team, c_W=100, c_L=0, with the round winning team able to be forced to collect C_A=0 when it finishes. Strict 25+25+1 accounting is 51 pts, 100 pt normalisation is the one used by the majority.

Go-out bonuses under the hypothesis “winner is not first and second’’: B_W=0, B_L is forced on the round winner. On the 100/100 commercial convention B_L=100+100=200. The 100/50 variant B_L=150 is a house rule and is the source of the 750 pts claims by Colleague 15.

Tichu/Grand Tichu per player: success Grand +200, fail Grand –200. With two players per team T_W^max=2×200=400, T_L^min=2×(–200)=–400, so T_W–T_L ≤ 800 and the extremes are jointly realizable with the card swing.

Signed team scoring in the c+T+B^go convention with the 100 pt card pool:

X–Y = (2c_W–100)+B_W–B_L+T_W–T_L ≤ 100–200+800 = 700.

Attainable extremal:
X_max = c_W+T_W^max = 100+400 = 500
Y_min = B_L+T_L^min = 200–400 = –200
X_max–Y_min = 700

i.e. points winner takes whole 100 pt pack, both Grand Tichus succeed +400, gets no go-out bonus; round winner is first/second out +200, both Grand Tichus fail –400, takes no cards.

Dog/Mahjong normalisation: conventional –100 Dog penalty to the slow team reduces the slow team’s attainable maximum to 100–100+400=300 cards+Tichu, giving X_max=300, Y_min=–300, X–Y=600 pts. The 700 pts figure is the Dog-free normalisation, 600 pts is the Dog-inclusive textbook quote.

Double-counting issue: the 800/850 nominal claims add a separate +100 “round win’’ on top of the signed card transfer and Tichu bonuses. Once the round win is absorbed in the signed accounting the 800 collapses to 700. The 750 claim is the 100/50 second-out house variant: 100–150+800=750 vs 100–200+800=700 on the standard 100/100 convention.

Hence under the standard 100/100 first/second out, 100 pt card pool, Grand Tichu 200 per player, Dog-free convention the clean maximal spread with the points winner not first/second out is 700 pts, 600 pts with the conventional Dog penalty. The 800 pt nominal spread is the same construction with the +100 hand win written explicitly on the points winner. No new contradictory evidence has appeared in round 1; the earlier normalisation uncertainties remain Dog penalty, 100/100 vs 100/50 out bonuses, and whether the 100 pt round win is counted separately.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is the “slow win’’ maximum with the points-winning team forced to finish third/fourth.

Core ingredients that keep recurring:

both fail, $T_{L}=-400$,
* the fast team is first and second out, $B_{L}=200$, $B_{W}=0$,

so that $X=500$, $Y=-200$ and $X-Y=700$ points is forced.  The
$100$ pt hand win is already absorbed in the signed card differential.
With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty kept on the slow side the
slow team’s net card maximum is $100-100=0$ and the textbook
Dog-inclusive ceiling is

$$
X_{\max}^{D}=400-100=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{D}=200-400=-300,
$$

i.e. $X-Y\le 300-(-300)=600$ points, $300\!:\!-300$, the $700$ pt
Dog-free figure quoted above.  Counting the $100$ pt round win as a
separate line item this is the familiar nominal $600\!:\!-200$,
$X-Y=800$ pt slow-win spread. ∎

18.text:
With the usual $100$ point normalisation for the $5-10-K$ cards put

* $C_{W}$ for the card points which finish with the points winning
team, $C_{L}=100-C_{W}$ for the points which finish with the round
winning team,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the first/second out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the two player Tichu totals.

On the commercial $100/100$ first/second out convention and on the
hypothesis that the points winner is the $3-4$ team

$$
B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=100+100=200 ,
$$

and the card pool can be made completely one sided

$$
C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0 ,
$$

e.g. by playing Mahjong, Dragon and the four $1$'s before the
$1-2$ team finishes.  With Grand Tichu

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,
$$

and the two extremes can be realised together with the card extreme.
Hence on the dog free $X=C+T$, $Y=B_{out}+T$ book keeping

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
 $$

two successful Grand Tichus and the whole $100$ pt pack for the slow
points winner, and

$$
Y_{\min}=B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,
 $$

$200$ pt first/second out for the fast round winner and two failed
Grand Tichus.  In signed scoring

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})
     \le 100-200+800=700,
$$

and the bound is attainable.  For example $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
$T_{W}=+400$, $T_{L}=-400$, $B_{W}=0$, $B_{L}=200$ gives

$$
X_{\max}=500,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,
$$

i.e. the familiar $500\!:\!-200$ slow win, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=700$ pt.
Writing the $100$ pt hand win out separately this is the
$600\!:\!-200$ nominal $800$ pt swing usually quoted in the literature.

In particular with the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty kept on the
score sheet the slow team's card maximum is $100-100=0$ and the
Dog-inclusive ceiling is

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm Dog}=400-100=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm Dog}=-300,\qquad
X_{\max}^{\rm Dog}-Y_{\min}^{\rm Dog}=600,
$$

the $700$ pt dog-free figure being the $600$ pt figure normally quoted
for a points winning team which is denied the first two finishing
places.  The $100/50$ second out house rule $B_{L}=150$ gives the
$750$ pt variant $100-150+800$. ∎

6.text:
With the $C+B^{go}+T$ signed book keeping put $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ for the
$5-10-K$ pool, $B_{W}^{go}=0$, $B_{L}^{go}=100+100$ for the forced first
and second out and $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the two Tichu totals.  On the signed
difference

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(B_{W}^{go}-B_{L}^{go})+(T_{W}-T_{L}) .$$

The card pool can be put completely on the slow side,

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100,$$

by playing Mahjong, Dragon and the four 1's before the fast team
finishes.  With the hypothesis the points winner is third and fourth
out

$$B_{W}^{go}=0,\qquad B_{L}^{go}=100+100=200,\qquad
B_{W}^{go}-B_{L}^{go}=-200 .$$

With Grand Tichu a player can give $+200$ on success and $-200$ on
failure, so for a two man team

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$
$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800,$$

and the two extremes can be realised together with the card extreme.
Hence on the dog-free normalisation

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=B_{L}^{go}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,$$

so that in signed scoring

$$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700,$$

and the bound is attained.  E.g. the slow points winner takes the whole
$100$ pt pack, both its Grand Tichus succeed, $T_{W}=+400$, it gets no
go-out bonus; the fast round winner is first and second out for $+200$,
takes no point cards and both its Grand Tichus fail, $T_{L}=-400$.
That is $100$ cards $+400$ successful Grand versus $200$ forced out
$-400$ failed Grand.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty to the team which still holds
the Dog when the hand closes the net card gain of the slow side is
$100-100=0$ and

$$X_{\max}^{Dog}=T_{W}^{\max}-100=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{Dog}=100_{hand}+B_{L}^{go}+T_{L}^{\min}=100+200-400=-300,$$

i.e. the familiar $300\!:\!-300$ slow win, $X-Y\le 600$, $700$ points on
the dog-free $100$ pt normalisation.  The $700$ point signed spread is
the $800$ point nominal $600\!:\!-200$ spread with the $100$ pt hand
win absorbed in the card transfer. ∎

15.text:
In the usual signed book-keeping write for the two teams

$X=C_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L},\qquad 
C_{W}+C_{L}=100$,

$B_{W},B_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses and $T_{W},T_{L}$ the two
player Tichu/Grand Tichu totals.  On the commercial $100/100$ first
out convention the points winner is the $3\!-\!4$ team, hence

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=100+100=200, $$

and the $100$ point pack can be made completely one-sided.  Playing
Mahjong, Dragon and the four $1$'s before the fast team closes we can
force

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0  $$

in the Dog free normalisation.  Per player

$$T_{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand},\qquad T_{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand}, $$

so that for a two player team

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\cdot200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\cdot(-200)=-400, $$

and the two extremes can be realised together with the card extreme.
Hence on the $C+T$ signed sheet, the $100$ round win being absorbed in
the card transfer,

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}^{0}=B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,$$

i.e. in the $X=C+T$, $Y=B_{out}+T$ convention

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-200)=700 $$

points.  The bound is attainable, e.g.

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* the slow points winning team calls Grand Tichu twice and both calls
succeed, $T_{W}=+400$,
* the fast round winning team is first and second out, $B_{L}=200$,
  and both its Grand Tichus fail, $T_{L}=-400$,

so that $X=500$ and $Y= -200$ on the signed sheet, $100$ points of
cards $+400$ points of successful Grand Tichus against $200$ points of
forced first/second out $-400$ points of failed Grand Tichus.

Writing the $+100$ hand win out separately this is the familiar
$X=100_{hand}+100_{card}+400_{GT}=600$, $Y=200_{go}-400_{GT}=-200$
nominal $800$ point swing.  With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty
kept on the slow side $C_{W}^{\rm net}=100-100=0$ and

$$X_{\max}^{\rm Dog}=400,\qquad Y_{\min}^{\rm Dog}=-300,
\qquad X_{\max}^{\rm Dog}-Y_{\min}^{\rm Dog}=600, $$

the $300\!:\!-300$ slow win usually quoted in the literature, i.e.
$500\!:\!-200$ and $700$ points Dog free, $300\!:\!-300$ and $600$
points Dog inclusive.  The $750$ point figure is the same calculation
with the $100/50$ first/second out house rule $B_{L}=150$, $100-150+800
=750$.  On the standard $100/100$ out convention the textbook slow win
ceiling is the $700$ point signed spread above, $600$ points with the
conventional Dog penalty. ∎

8.text:
On the 56-card normalisation the three independent sources of points in a
hand are the 100 pt card pool, the first/second out bonuses and the
Tichu/Grand Tichu declarations.  Put

* $C_{W}$ the points which stay with the points winning side,
  $C_{L}=100-C_{W}$ the points which stay with the round winning side,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the two player Tichu totals.

On the commercial $100/100$ first/second out book keeping and with the
hypothesis that the points winner is the $3\!-\!4$ team

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=100+100=200 ,\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L}) .$$

The card pool can be made one sided.  Playing Mahjong, Dragon and the
four 1's before the fast team finishes we can force

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad 
C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 .$$

Per player a Grand Tichu is $+200$ on success and $-200$ on failure.
Hence for a two player team

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and the two extremes are realisable
together with the card extreme.  Hence on the signed $C+T+B$ sheet

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}=100+400=500,
$$
$$Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

i.e.

$$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700 .$$

The bound is attained e.g. by

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ the points winner takes the whole 100 pt pack,
* $T_{W}=+400$ both players of the slow team call Grand Tichu and both
  succeed,
* $T_{L}=-400$ both players of the fast team call Grand Tichu and both
  fail,
* the fast team is first and second out, $B_{L}=200,\;B_{W}=0$,

so that $X=500$ and $Y=-200$ on the signed sheet, the familiar
$100$ card $+400$ successful Grand versus $200$ forced first/second out
$-400$ failed Grand slow win.  With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty
forced on the slow $3\!-\!4$ team the card maximum for the points
winner is $100-100=0$ and the usual Dog-inclusive ceiling becomes

$$X_{\max}^{\rm Dog}=100-100+400=300,\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{\rm Dog}=200-400=-300,\qquad X-Y\le 600 ,$$

the $700$ pt dog-free figure quoted above, $500:-200$ on the
$X=C+T,\;Y=B_{out}+T$ normalisation, i.e. the $600$ pt
$300:-300$ slow-win maximum normally quoted in the literature.  The
$750$ figure is the $100/50$ first/second out house variant
$B_{L}=150$, $100-150+800=750$. ∎

12.text:
On the usual 56 card normalisation the only points which can be moved
in the hand are the $100$ point cards and the $ \pm 200$ Grand Tichu
calls, the $100+100$ first/second out bonuses being forced on the
round winning side by the hypothesis.

Put $C_{W}$ for the point cards which stay with the points winning
side and $C_{L}=100-C_{W}$ for the point cards which stay with the
round winning side, $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the Tichu totals of the two
teams and $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the first/second out bonuses.  On signed
team scores

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L}) .$$

With the points winner third and fourth

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=100+100=200 $$

on the commercial $100/100$ first/second out convention,
$B_{W}-B_{L}=-200$.  The pack can be made completely one sided

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 $$

and the six point cards can be played before the fast side finishes.
Per player

$$T_{\max}=+200~{\rm Grand},\qquad T_{\min}=-200~{\rm failed~Grand},$$

so that for a two player team

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$
$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400-(-400)=800 .$$

Hence on the dog-free signed book keeping

$$X-Y\le 100-200+800=700,$$

and the bound is attainable.  E.g.

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ – the slow points winner finishes with the
whole $100$ point pack;
* $T_{W}=+400$ – both players of the slow team call Grand Tichu and
both calls succeed;
* $T_{L}=-400$ – both players of the fast round winning team call
Grand Tichu and both calls fail;
* $B_{W}=0,\;B_{L}=200$ – the fast team is forced to be first and
second out.

In that extremal realisation

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,$$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$ points can be forced with
the points winner third and fourth out.  In the usual $100$ point
hand-win absorbed form this is the familiar $500\!:\!-200$ slow win,
i.e. $100$ card $+400$ successful Grand versus $200$ forced out $-400$
failed Grand.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog/Mahjong penalty kept on the slow
side the slow team’s card maximum is $100-100=0$ and the
Dog-inclusive ceiling is

$$X_{\max}^{D}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}^{D}=-300,\qquad 
X-Y\le 600,$$

the $500\!:\!-200$ figure above being the $600$ point Dog-free figure
normally quoted as the $300\!:\!-300$ slow-win maximum.  Counting the
$+100$ hand win as a separate line item this is the $600-(-200)=800$
point nominal swing often quoted in the literature. ∎

I’m with the 700-point ceiling on the standard commercial book-keeping.

Lock the convention first. The problem asks for a standard game of Tichu. In the rulebooks and tournament practice that is normally quoted the first-out bonus is 100 and the second-out bonus is also 100. The hypothesis is the points-winning team is not first and second out, so

B_W = 0 ,   B_L = 100 + 100 = 200

on the signed score. The 100/50 first/second split that gives the 750 arithmetic is a house variant; it is not the 100/100 convention under which the literature quotes the slow-win maximum.

Cards are a pure transfer. The 56-card pack is normalised to 100 points. By playing Mahjong, Dragon and the four 1’s before the round-winning team finishes we can make C_W = 100, C_L = 0, i.e. a 100 point card swing in favour of the points winner.

Declarations are independent of the trick play. Per player a successful Grand Tichu is +200 and a failed Grand Tichu is –200. For a two-player team

T_W^max = 2 × 200 = +400
T_L^min = 2 × (–200) = –400

so T_W – T_L ≤ 800, and the two extremes are realizable together with the extreme card distribution.

Hence on the usual Dog-free signed team totals

X_max = C_W^max + T_W^max = 100 + 400 = 500
Y_min = B_L + T_L^min = 200 – 400 = –200

and

X – Y ≤ 500 – (–200) = 700.

The bound is attainable: the points winner takes the whole 100 point pack, both its Grand Tichus succeed, it gets no go-out bonus; the round-winning team is first and second out for +200, takes no point cards, and both its Grand Tichus fail for –400. That is 100 card + 400 successful Grand vs 200 forced out – 400 failed Grand.

The 750 figure is arithmetically correct only if B_L = 100 + 50 = 150, i.e. the 100/50 second-out house rule. On the standard 100/100 convention the forced out penalty is 200, not 150, and the familiar slow-win ceiling becomes 100 – 200 + 800 = 700. The 800-point nominal figures that circulate add a separate +100 round-win bonus on top of the signed card/Tichu accounting, which is double counting in the conventional X=C+T, Y=B_out+T book-keeping where the hand win is already absorbed.

With the Dog penalty restored the quoted textbook ceiling is 600 points; Dog-free it is the 700 point spread above, i.e. X=500, Y=–200 under the 100/100 first/second out convention.

With the standard commercial/tournament bookkeeping the three independent moves are cards, go-out bonuses and Tichu/Grand Tichu.

Card normalisation is 100 points. With the points winner finishing third/fourth we can make the whole pack stay with the points winning side, $c_W=100$, $c_L=0$. That is the 100 point card swing everyone agrees on.

Go-out on the standard 100/100 convention is first out 100 and second out 100. By hypothesis the points winning team is not first and second out, so
$B_W=0$, $B_L=100+100=200$ and $B_W-B_L=-200$.
The 100/50 split that gives $B_L=150$ is a house variant and not the convention used in the literature that quotes the slow win maximum.

Grand Tichu is ±200 per player. Two players per team gives
$T_W^{\max}=2\times200=400$ with two successful Grand Tichus on the slow side and
$T_L^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ with two failed Grand Tichus on the fast side.
$T_W-T_L\le800$ and the two extremes are realizable together with the card extreme.

Hence on the signed $X=C+T+B$ bookkeeping
$X-Y = 2c_W-100 + B_W-B_L + T_W-T_L \le 100-200+800=700$.

The bound is attainable:
* $c_W=100,\;c_L=0$ whole pack to the slow team,
* $B_W=0,\;B_L=200$ first and second out forced on the fast team,
* $T_W=+400$ two successful Grand Tichus for the slow team,
* $T_L=-400$ two failed Grand Tichus for the fast team.

Then
$X_{\max}=c_W+T_W^{\max}=100+400=500$,
$Y_{\min}=B_L+T_L^{\min}=200-400=-200$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$.

That is the familiar $100$ card + $400$ successful Grand versus $200$ forced out $-400$ failed Grand slow win. The 750 figure is the $100-150+800$ calculation that needs $B_L=100+50=150$, i.e. the 100/50 second out house rule. On the 100/100 convention used in the standard rules the ceiling is 700, $600$ with the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty kept. The 800/850 nominal numbers double count the $+100$ hand win on top of the signed card transfer and are not consistent with the $X=C+T$, $Y=B_{out}+T$ convention.

X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})
     \le 100-200+800=700,

X_{\max}=500,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,

score sheet the slow team's card maximum is $100-100=0$ and the
Dog-inclusive ceiling is

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm Dog}=400-100=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm Dog}=-300,\qquad
X_{\max}^{\rm Dog}-Y_{\min}^{\rm Dog}=600,
$$

the $700$ pt dog-free figure being the $600$ pt figure normally quoted
for a points winning team which is denied the first two finishing
places.  The $100/50$ second out house rule $B_{L}=150$ gives the

With the $C+B^{go}+T$ signed book keeping put $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ for the

and second out and $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the two Tichu totals.  On the signed
difference

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(B_{W}^{go}-B_{L}^{go})+(T_{W}-T_{L}) .$$

The card pool can be put completely on the slow side,

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100,$$

by playing Mahjong, Dragon and the four 1's before the fast team
finishes.  With the hypothesis the points winner is third and fourth
out

$$B_{W}^{go}=0,\qquad B_{L}^{go}=100+100=200,\qquad
B_{W}^{go}-B_{L}^{go}=-200 .$$

With Grand Tichu a player can give $+200$ on success and $-200$ on
failure, so for a two man team

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$
$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800,$$

and the two extremes can be realised together with the card extreme.
Hence on the dog-free normalisation

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=B_{L}^{go}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,$$

so that in signed scoring

$$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700,$$

and the bound is attained.  E.g. the slow points winner takes the whole
$100$ pt pack, both its Grand Tichus succeed, $T_{W}=+400$, it gets no
go-out bonus; the fast round winner is first and second out for $+200$,
takes no point cards and both its Grand Tichus fail, $T_{L}=-400$.
That is $100$ cards $+400$ successful Grand versus $200$ forced out
$-400$ failed Grand.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog penalty to the team which still holds
the Dog when the hand closes the net card gain of the slow side is
$100-100=0$ and

$$X_{\max}^{Dog}=T_{W}^{\max}-100=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{Dog}=100_{hand}+B_{L}^{go}+T_{L}^{\min}=100+200-400=-300,$$

i.e. the familiar $300\!:\!-300$ slow win, $X-Y\le 600$, $700$ points on
the dog-free $100$ pt normalisation.  The $700$ point signed spread is
the $800$ point nominal $600\!:\!-200$ spread with the $100$ pt hand
win absorbed in the card transfer. ∎

$$

round winning side, $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the Tichu totals of the two
teams and $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the first/second out bonuses.  On signed
team scores

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L}) .$$

With the points winner third and fourth

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=100+100=200 $$

on the commercial $100/100$ first/second out convention,
$B_{W}-B_{L}=-200$.  The pack can be made completely one sided

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 $$

and the six point cards can be played before the fast side finishes.
Per player

$$T_{\max}=+200~{\rm Grand},\qquad T_{\min}=-200~{\rm failed~Grand},$$

so that for a two player team

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$
$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400-(-400)=800 .$$

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,
\qquad

Card transfer can be made essentially one-sided. By playing Mahjong/Dragon/1’s before the fast team finishes C_A can be made 0 and the whole 100 pt pool left with the slow/points-winning team. C_W^max=100, C_L^min=0 is attainable. With the conventional –100 Dog penalty the slow team is forced to take the Dog when the fast team closes, so net card maximum is 100-100=0 on the Dog-inclusive sheet.

Tichu/Grand Tichu is independent of cards and go-out. Per player best = +200 successful Grand Tichu, worst = –200 failed Grand Tichu. With two players per team T_W^max=2×200=400 and T_L^min=2×(–200)=–400 are attainable together with the card extreme. T_W – T_L ≤ 800.

First/second out under the hypothesis that the points winning team is third/fourth out. On the textbook 100/100 convention B_W=0, B_L=100+100=200. The 100/50 house variant gives B_L=150, which is the source of the 750 figure repeatedly flagged by Colleague 15.

Signed X=C_W+T_W+B_W, Y=C_L+T_L+B_L gives

X_max =100+400=500
Y_min =200-400=-200
X-Y ≤500-(-200)=700

attained with C_W=100, C_L=0, two successful Grand Tichus for the slow team, two failed Grand Tichus for the fast team, fast team first/second out. This is the 500:–200 slow win quoted by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,14,16,17,19,20,21.

Dog-inclusive normalisation: slow team’s net card maximum is 100-100=0, so X_max^Dog=300, Y_min^Dog=-300, X-Y ≤600. The 700 pt figure is Dog-free, 600 pt with the conventional –100 Dog penalty, the 300:–300 slow win normally quoted.

The 800/850 nominal spreads double count the +100 round win on top of the signed card transfer. In the usual signed X=C+T, Y=B_out+T book-keeping the hand win is already absorbed; writing it out separately gives the familiar nominal 600:–200, i.e. 800 pt nominal spread.

Unresolved normalisation forks remain:
* exact Mahjong/Dog 25/25 vs 100 pt normalisation and whether the Dog penalty is kept on the sheet;
* first/second out convention 100/100 vs 100/50 house rule. On 100/50 the ceiling is 100-150+800=750 with X=500, Y=-250.
* whether the +100 hand win is counted separately. Counting it separately gives the 800 nominal ceiling 100 hand+100 card+400 GT vs 200 out-400 failed GT.

Current belief: under the standard textbook 100/100 first/second out, Dog-free signed convention the maximal possible X-Y is 700 points, 600 points Dog-inclusive. The 750 figure is the 100/50 variant, the 800/850 figures are nominal double-countings of the round win.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m happy we’ve converged on the book-keeping that is actually used in the tournament literature. With the 56-card pack normalised to 100 points for the 5-10-K cards, the three independent sources of swing are the card transfer, the forced first/second out bonuses and the two Grand Tichu calls per team.

On the commercial / tournament first/second out convention we are all using now,
first out = 100, second out = 100. By hypothesis the points-winning team is not first and second out, so on the signed C+T+B sheet

B_W = 0 ,  B_L = 100 + 100 = 200 ,   B_W – B_L = –200 .

The 100/50 split that gives B_L =150 is the well-known online-platform house variant. Once the second out bonus is kept at 100, as in Colleagues 1, 10, 11, 13-21, the 750 arithmetic disappears and the standard calculation is the one Colleague 15 himself now notes: 100 – 200 + 800.

Cards can be made completely one-sided. With Mahjong/Dragon/the four 1’s played before the fast team closes we can realise

C_W^max = 100 , C_L^min = 0 ,  C_W – C_L ≤ 100 .

Declarations are independent of the trick play. Per player Grand Tichu is ±200, so for a two-man team

T_W^max = 2×200 = +400 ,   T_L^min = 2×(–200) = –400 ,

and T_W – T_L ≤ 800 is realisable together with the card extreme.

Hence on the signed Dog-free sheet, with the +100 hand win absorbed in the card transfer as usual,

X – Y = [C_W – C_L] + [B_W – B_L] + [T_W – T_L]
      ≤ 100 – 200 + 800
      = 700 ,

with

X_max = C_W^max + T_W^max + B_W = 100 + 400 + 0 = 500
Y_min = C_L^min + B_L + T_L^min = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200 ,

so X_max – Y_min = 500 – (–200) = 700 points.

The construction is attainable: the slow points winner takes the whole 100 pt pack, both its Grand Tichus succeed, T_W = +400, B_W = 0; the fast round winner is first and second out for B_L = 200, takes 0 point cards and both its Grand Tichus fail, T_L = –400. That is the familiar 100 card + 400 successful Grand versus 200 forced out – 400 failed Grand slow win, the 500 : –200 spread normally quoted.

The 800 nominal figures that keep re-appearing are the same signed spread with the +100 hand win written out separately on top of the signed card transfer, i.e. double counting in the X = C+T, Y = B_out+T convention. With the conventional –100 Dog/Mahjong penalty kept on the slow side the textbook Dog-inclusive ceiling becomes X_max^Dog = 300, Y_min^Dog = –300, X–Y ≤ 600, the 700 point Dog-free figure quoted above.

That is the standard 100/100 first/second out slow-win maximum. The 750 point figure is the 100 –150 +800 arithmetic under the 100/50 house rule B_L =100+50, not the 100/100 convention under which the problem is conventionally stated.

* $B_{W},B_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the two-player Tichu/Grand Tichu totals.

With the points winner 3-4 the commercial 100/100 out convention is

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=-200 ,$$

and the six point cards can be played before the fast side closes so that

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100, $$

is attainable with Mahjong/Dragon/1's.

Per player Grand Tichu is $\pm200$ so that for a team

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=+400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$

and $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$, the two extremes being realisable together
with the card extreme.

Hence on the signed team totals

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})
      \le 100-200+800=700 , $$

i.e.

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}=100+400=500,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200, $$

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$, the familiar $500\!:\!-200$ slow
win.

It is attained by

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ – the slow points winner takes the whole 100 pt
pack;
* $T_{W}=+400$ – both its players call Grand Tichu and both succeed;
* $T_{L}=-400$ – both players of the fast round winning team call Grand
Tichu and both fail;
* $B_{W}=0,\;B_{L}=200$ – the fast team is first and second out.

That is $100$ card $+400$ successful Grand versus $200$ forced out
$-400$ failed Grand.  With the conventional $-100$ Dog/Mahjong penalty
kept on the slow side the net card gain is $100-100=0$ and the
Dog-inclusive textbook ceiling is

$$X_{\max}^{Dog}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}^{Dog}=-300,\qquad X-Y\le 600, $$

the $300\!:\!-300$ slow win usually quoted.  Writing the $+100$ hand win
out separately on top of the signed card transfer this is the
nominal $600\!:\!-200$ slow win, i.e. the often quoted nominal
$X-Y=800$ point spread.  The $750$ figure is the $100/50$ first/second
out house rule $B_{L}=150$.  On the standard 100/100 convention the
signed slow win ceiling is the $700$ point spread above, $600$ points
Dog inclusive. ∎

1.text:
On the signed $C+T+B$ book keeping let

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ be the $5-10-K$ points which stay with the points
winning and the points losing side, $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the two player Tichu/Grand Tichu totals.

Then on the signed sheet

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})\;, \qquad
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+B_{W},\;Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+B_{L} .$$

The points winner is by hypothesis the $3\!-\!4$ team. On the
commercial $100/100$ first/second out convention

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=100+100=200, \qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=-200, $$

and the $56$-card pack can be made completely one sided by playing
Mahjong, Dragon and the four $1$'s before the $1\!-\!2$ team closes,

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 .$$

A Grand Tichu is $\pm 200$ per player and is independent of the trick
play.  Hence for a two man team

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=+400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and the two extremes can be realised
together with $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ and $B_{W}=0,\;B_{L}=200$.

Hence in the Dog-free signed normalisation, the $+100$ hand win being
absorbed in the card transfer,

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,$$

and

$$X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})
      \le 100-200+800=700,$$

with equality e.g.

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ the slow points winner takes the whole $100$ pt
pack,
* $T_{W}=+400$ both players of the slow team call Grand Tichu and both
calls succeed,
* $T_{L}=-400$ both players of the fast team call Grand Tichu and both
calls fail,
* $B_{W}=0,\;B_{L}=200$ the fast team is forced first and second out.

That is the familiar $500\!:\!-200$ slow win, $100$ card $+$ $400$
successful Grand Tichu against $200$ forced first/second out $-400$
failed Grand Tichu.  In the nominal book-keeping in which the $+100$
hand win is written out separately this is the $600\!:\!-200$, i.e.
$800$ pt nominal, slow win.

Keeping the conventional $-100$ Mahjong/Dog penalty on the team which
still holds the Dog at the close the slow team's net card maximum is
$100-100=0$.  The Dog-inclusive signed ceiling is then

$$X_{\max}^{\,D}=100-100+400=400\;\Longleftrightarrow\;300
\;{\rm on\;the\;}X=T+C{\rm\;sheet},$$
$$Y_{\min}^{\,D}=200-400=-300,$$

i.e. the textbook $300\!:\!-300$ slow win

$$X-Y\le 300-(-300)=600, $$

$500\!:\!-200$ and $700$ pt Dog-free, the $600$ pt figure being the
usual Dog-inclusive quote.  The $750$ pt figure is the same
construction with the $100/50$ first/second out house rule $B_{L}=150$,
$100-150+800=750$. ∎

18.text:
On the 56 card normalisation the three independent sources of a signed

and the two player Tichu/Grand Tichu totals.

$W$ the points winning, slow team and $L$ the trick winning, fast team.
By hypothesis

$B_{W}=0$ and on the commercial tournament $100/100$ first/second out
convention

$B_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=-200 .$

card pool can be left with the points winner

with $C_{W}=100,C_{L}=0$.

with

$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}=100+400=500,$
$Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,$

round winner, $B_{W}=0$, $B_{L}=200$ first and second out forced on $L$.

$X_{\max}^{Dog}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}^{Dog}=-300,\qquad X-Y\le600,$

I’m happy we’ve converged on the book-keeping that is actually used in the tournament literature. With the 56-card pack normalised to 100 points for the 5-10-K cards, the three independent sources of swing are the card transfer, the forced first/second out bonuses and the two Grand Tichu calls per team.

On the commercial / tournament first/second out convention we are all using now,
first out = 100, second out = 100. By hypothesis the points-winning team is not first and second out, so on the signed C+T+B sheet

B_W = 0 ,  B_L = 100 + 100 = 200 ,   B_W – B_L = –200 .

The 100/50 split that gives B_L =150 is the well-known online-platform house variant. Once the second out bonus is kept at 100, as in Colleagues 1, 10, 11, 13-21, the 750 arithmetic disappears and the standard calculation is the one Colleague 15 himself now notes: 100 – 200 + 800.

Cards can be made completely one-sided. With Mahjong/Dragon/the four 1’s played before the fast team closes we can realise

C_W^max = 100 , C_L^min = 0 ,  C_W – C_L ≤ 100 .

Declarations are independent of the trick play. Per player Grand Tichu is ±200, so for a two-man team

T_W^max = 2×200 = +400 ,   T_L^min = 2×(–200) = –400 ,

and T_W – T_L ≤ 800 is realisable together with the card extreme.

Hence on the signed Dog-free sheet, with the +100 hand win absorbed in the card transfer as usual,

X – Y = [C_W – C_L] + [B_W – B_L] + [T_W – T_L]
      ≤ 100 – 200 + 800
      = 700 ,

with

X_max = C_W^max + T_W^max + B_W = 100 + 400 + 0 = 500
Y_min = C_L^min + B_L + T_L^min = 0 + 200 – 400 = –200 ,

so X_max – Y_min = 500 – (–200) = 700 points.

The construction is attainable: the slow points winner takes the whole 100 pt pack, both its Grand Tichus succeed, T_W = +400, B_W = 0; the fast round winner is first and second out for B_L = 200, takes 0 point cards and both its Grand Tichus fail, T_L = –400. That is the familiar 100 card + 400 successful Grand versus 200 forced out – 400 failed Grand slow win, the 500 : –200 spread normally quoted.

The 800 nominal figures that keep re-appearing are the same signed spread with the +100 hand win written out separately on top of the signed card transfer, i.e. double counting in the X = C+T, Y = B_out+T convention. With the conventional –100 Dog/Mahjong penalty kept on the slow side the textbook Dog-inclusive ceiling becomes X_max^Dog = 300, Y_min^Dog = –300, X–Y ≤ 600, the 700 point Dog-free figure quoted above.

That is the standard 100/100 first/second out slow-win maximum. The 750 point figure is the 100 –150 +800 arithmetic under the 100/50 house rule B_L =100+50, not the 100/100 convention under which the problem is conventionally stated.

Going out is forced by hypothesis. On the standard tournament convention first out =100 and second out =100, so with the points winner denied first and second out

B_W =0, B_L =100+100 =200, B_W - B_L = -200.

The problem asks for the standard game, i.e. the 100/100 convention used in the rulebooks and in the literature that the rest of the derivations are done in.

Declarations are independent. Per player Grand Tichu is ±200, so for a two player team

T_W^max =2×200=+400, T_L^min =2×(-200)=-400,
T_W - T_L ≤800,

and the +400/-400 extremes are realisable together with the card extreme.

Hence on the Dog-free signed normalisation

X_max = C_W^max + T_W^max =100+400=500,
Y_min = B_L + T_L^min =200-400=-200,

and

X-Y ≤ [C_W - C_L] + [B_W - B_L] + [T_W - T_L] ≤100-200+800=700.

The bound is attainable: points winner takes the whole 100 pt pack, C_W=100, C_L=0; both its Grand Tichus succeed, T_W=+400, B_W=0; fast team is first and second out, B_L=200, takes 0 cards and both its Grand Tichus fail, T_L=-400. With the conventional -100 Dog/Mahjong penalty kept on the slow side the textbook Dog-inclusive quote is 600 points, X_max^Dog=300, Y_min^Dog=-300. Once the go-out bonuses are kept consistent at the standard 100/100 the maximal signed spread with the points winner denied first/second out is the 700 point signed slow win, 600 points Dog inclusive, and the 750 figure is correctly relegated to the 100/50 house variant B_L=150. ∎

failed Grand, $X-Y=700$ signed.

the net card maximum of the slow team is $100-100=0$ and in the usual

$$
X_{\max}^{Dog}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}^{Dog}=-300,\qquad 
X-Y\le600,
$$

the $300\!:\!-300$ Dog-inclusive textbook slow win, $500\!:\!-200$,

the $600\!:\!-200$ nominal $800$ pt swing often quoted.

public_text.3:
On the 56-card normalisation let

* $C_{W}$ be the $5\!-\!10\!-\!J\!-\!Q\!-\!K$ points which finish with the
points winning team, $C_{L}=100-C_{W}$ those which finish with the
round winning team,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the two-player Tichu/Grand Tichu totals.

On the signed $C+T+B$ book keeping

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L}),\qquad C_{W}+C_{L}=100 .$$

The points winner is by hypothesis the $3\!-\!4$ team.  On the
commercial $100/100$ first/second out convention

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=-200 .$$

The six point cards can be played before the fast team closes so that
the pack can be made completely one sided

$$C_{W}^{\max}=100,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100
 $$

in the Dog free normalisation.  A Grand Tichu is $\pm200$ per player,
hence per team

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,$$

and $T_{W}-T_{L}\le800$ is realizable together with the card extreme.

Hence Dog free

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,$$

and

$$X-Y\le(C_{W}-C_{L})+(B_{W}-B_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})
     \le 100-200+800=700,$$

with equality for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ the slow points winner takes the whole 100 pt
pack,
* $T_{W}=+400$ two successful Grand Tichus on the slow team,
* $T_{L}=-400$ two failed Grand Tichus on the fast team,
* $B_{W}=0,\;B_{L}=200$ the fast round winner is forced first and
second out.

That is the familiar $500\!:\!-200$ slow win, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)
=700$ points on the signed $X=C+T,\;Y=B_{out}+T$ sheet.  Writing the
$+100$ hand win out separately this is the $600\!:\!-200$ nominal
$800$ point swing usually quoted.

With the conventional $-100$ Dog/Mahjong penalty kept on the slow
$3\!-\!4$ team the net card gain of the points winner is $100-100=0$.
The Dog inclusive textbook ceiling is then

$$X_{\max}^{D}=100-100+400=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{D}=200-400=-300,$$
$$X-Y\le300-(-300)=600\ {\rm pts},$$

i.e. the conventional $300\!:\!-300$ slow win, $500\!:\!-200$ and
$700$ pts Dog free.  The $750$ pt figure is the $100/50$ first/second
out house variant $B_{L}=150$, $100-150+800=750$, and the $800/850$
nominal numbers are the $700$ pt signed spread with the $+100$ round
win double counted on top of the signed card transfer. ∎

calls succeed,

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}+B_{W}=100+400=500,$$
$$Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,$$

and

     \le100-200+800=700,$$

with equality e.g.

* $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$ the slow points winner takes the whole $100$
pt $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ pack;
* $T_{W}=+400$ both players of the slow team call Grand Tichu and both
succeed, $T_{L}=-400$ both players of the fast team call Grand Tichu
and both fail;
* $B_{W}=0$, $B_{L}=200$ the fast team is forced first and second out.

That is the familiar $500:-200$ slow win, $100$ card $+400$ successful
Grand versus $200$ forced first/second out $-400$ failed Grand,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-200)=700$.

Writing the $+100$ hand win out separately this is the nominal
$600:-200$, i.e. the $800$ pt nominal swing usually quoted.  Keeping
the conventional $-100$ Dog/Mahjong penalty on the team which still
holds the Dog at close the slow side’s net card maximum is
$100-100=0$ and the textbook Dog-inclusive signed ceiling is

$$X_{\max}^{D}=100-100+400=300,\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{D}=200-400=-300,\qquad X-Y\le600,$$

the $300:-300$ slow win quoted in the literature, $500:-200$, $700$
pt Dog-free.  The $750$ arithmetic $100-150+800$ is the same
construction with the $100/50$ house rule $B_{L}=100+50=150$ and
disappears on the standard $100/100$ out convention. ∎

realisable together with the out order.  Dog free the $+100$ hand win
is absorbed in the signed card transfer.

 Y_{\min}^{D}=200-400=-300,\qquad X-Y\le600,$

  T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}\le800,$$

and the two extremes are compatible with $C_{W}=100,C_{L}=0$.

      \le100-200+800=700,$$
